where Śrī Rāma, the crest-jewel of all the gods, became incarnate?
bal.298.cau1: Then the king summoned Bharata and said: Go and make ready the horses, elephants and chariots,
and set out quickly in Śrī Rāma's wedding procession. On hearing this, both brothers thrilled with joy.
bal.298.cau2: Bharata called all the masters of the stables and gave his orders; they rose gladly and hurried off.
They fitted the horses with saddles chosen with care, and fine steeds of every colour stood resplendent.
bal.298.cau3: All are handsome and exceedingly lively in their paces; they set their hooves to the ground as if it were red-hot iron.
They are of many breeds, beyond describing, and seem to scorn the wind and long to fly.
bal.298.cau4: On them all mounted dashing princes of Bharata's own age,
all handsome, all wearing ornaments, with bows and arrows in their hands and heavy quivers at their waists.
bal.298.do298: All are picked youths, handsome and dashing, brave, accomplished and young;
with each rider go two foot soldiers skilled in the art of the sword.
bal.299.cau1: Wearing their badges of valour, those heroes, staunch in battle, came out and stood outside the city.
Skilled riders, they wheel their horses through many paces and rejoice as they hear the drums and kettledrums.
bal.299.cau2: The charioteers made the chariots wonderful, fitting them with flags, pennants, gems and ornaments.
Lovely fly-whisks adorn them and little bells tinkle, and they rob the Sun's chariot of its splendour.
bal.299.cau3: There were countless black-eared horses, and the charioteers yoked them to those chariots.
All handsome and richly adorned, they look splendid; the sight of them charms even the minds of sages.
bal.299.cau4: They run on water as on land, and so great is their speed that their hooves do not sink.
Having made ready all the weapons, missiles and gear, the charioteers called the chariot-warriors.
bal.299.do299: Mounting their chariots one after another, the procession began to gather outside the city.
Whoever sets out on whatever errand, fine omens appear for all.
bal.300.cau1: Lovely howdahs were set on the noble elephants, adorned in a way that words cannot tell.
The elephants in rut moved off, splendid with their bells, like lovely banks of clouds in the month of Śrāvaṇa.
bal.300.cau2: There were other conveyances of many kinds: lovely palanquins, litters and carriages.
Mounted on them, hosts of eminent Brahmins went along, as if all the metres of the Vedas had taken bodily form.
bal.300.cau3: Bards, chroniclers, heralds and singers of praise went along, each mounted on the vehicle that befitted him.
Mules, camels and bullocks of many kinds went, laden with goods of countless sorts.
bal.300.cau4: Bearers by the million went with loads slung from their poles; who could describe all the things of every kind?
All the throngs of servants went as well, each with his own gear and his own company arranged.
bal.300.do300: Every heart brims with joy, and every body thrills:
When shall we feast our eyes on Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the two heroes?
bal.301.cau1: Elephants trumpet and bells clang fearsomely; chariots rumble and horses neigh on every side.
Kettledrums thunder, putting the clouds to shame, and no word, one's own or another's, can be heard.
bal.301.cau2: At the king's gate the crowd is so dense that a stone thrown into it would be ground to dust.
Women on the balconies look on, holding auspicious trays with lamps for the āratī,
bal.301.cau3: and sing charming songs of many kinds; their great joy is beyond describing.
Then Sumantra made ready two chariots and yoked to them horses that put the Sun's own steeds to shame.
bal.301.cau4: He brought the two lovely chariots to the king; not even Sarasvatī could describe them.
One chariot was arrayed with the royal trappings; the other, a mass of splendour, shone exceedingly.
bal.301.do301: The king joyfully seated Vasiṣṭha in that lovely chariot,
and, remembering Śiva, his guru, Gaurī and Gaṇeśa, mounted a chariot himself.
bal.302.cau1: How does the king look beside Vasiṣṭha? Like Indra beside Bṛhaspati, the guru of the gods.
Having performed the rites by family custom and Vedic rule, and having seen everyone and every arrangement in order,
bal.302.cau2: the king remembered Śrī Rāma, received the guru's leave, and set out with the sounding of conches.
The gods rejoiced to see the procession, and, givers of every blessing, they rained down flowers.
bal.302.cau3: A great clamour arose, horses and elephants cried out, and music sounded in the sky and in the procession.
The women of gods and of men sang songs of blessing, and the shehnais played sweet melodies.
bal.302.cau4: The ringing of bells great and small is past describing; the foot soldiers show off their feats and leap about.
Jesters play pranks of many kinds, skilled at raising laughter and accomplished in sweet song.
bal.302.do302: Fine princes make their horses dance to the sound of the mṛdaṅga and the kettledrums,
and skilled dancers watch in amazement as the horses never once stray from the measure of the beat.
bal.303.cau1: The procession was formed so finely that it is beyond describing. Beautiful omens that bring good fortune appear.
On the left a blue jay is picking up its food, as if announcing every blessing.
bal.303.cau2: On the right a crow in a fine field is a pleasing sight, and everyone caught sight of a mongoose.
The threefold breeze, cool, gentle and fragrant, blows favourably; a fine woman comes by with a pitcher and a child.
bal.303.cau3: Time and again a fox turned to show itself, and before them a cow was suckling her calf.
A herd of deer wheeled round to the right, as though all the hosts of blessings had come into view.
bal.303.cau4: The kṣemakarī bird foretells especial good fortune, and a śyāmā bird was seen on the left on a fine tree.
Curd and fish came before them, and two learned Brahmins with books in their hands.
bal.303.do303: All were auspicious, full of blessing and givers of the desired fruit,
as though every omen had appeared at once in order to come true.
bal.304.cau1: All auspicious omens come easily to one whose beautiful sons are Brahman with attributes.
The bridegroom is such a one as Śrī Rāma, the bride is Sītā, and the fathers joined by the marriage are the holy Daśaratha and Janaka.
bal.304.cau2: Hearing of such a wedding, all the omens danced: now Brahmā has made us come true.
In this way the procession set out; horses and elephants roared, and the kettledrums were beaten.
bal.304.cau3: Knowing that Daśaratha, the banner of the solar race, was coming, Janaka had bridges built over the rivers.
At stages along the way he had fine lodgings made, filled with riches like those of the city of the gods.
bal.304.cau4: There everyone received fine food, beds and lovely clothes, each to his own liking.
Seeing comforts new each day and suited to them, all the members of the procession forgot their homes.
bal.304.do304: Knowing that the splendid procession was near, and hearing the kettledrums booming,
the welcoming party made ready elephants, chariots, foot soldiers and horses and went out to receive it.
bal.305.cau1: Golden pitchers, great platters and trays, and lovely vessels of many kinds
were filled with every delicacy, each like nectar, of so many sorts that they cannot be described.
bal.305.cau2: Many fruits and other fine and lovely things the king joyfully sent as gifts,
with ornaments, clothes, precious gems of many kinds, birds, beasts, horses, elephants and carriages of every sort.
bal.305.cau3: The king sent auspicious things of good omen and lovely perfumes of many kinds.
Bearers set off with their carrying-poles loaded full of curd, flattened rice and gifts beyond count.
bal.305.cau4: When the welcoming party saw the procession, their hearts filled with joy and their bodies thrilled.
Seeing the welcomers in all their array, the members of the procession joyfully beat their kettledrums.
bal.305.do305: Joyfully, to meet one another, some rode forward abreast, rein to rein,
as if two oceans of joy were meeting, leaving their shores behind.
bal.306.cau1: The fair women of heaven shower flowers and sing, and the gods joyfully sound their drums.
The welcomers set all the gifts before King Daśaratha and made their humble request with great affection.
bal.306.cau2: The king accepted it all with love, and then it was given away as largesse to the suppliants.
Then, with worship, honour and praise, the welcomers led them to the lodging prepared for the procession.
bal.306.cau3: Cloths of many colours are spread as carpets along the way; seeing them, Kubera gives up his pride in his wealth.
A most beautiful lodging was given to the procession, where everyone had every comfort.
bal.306.cau4: When Sītā knew that the procession had come to the city, she revealed a little of her own glory.
Remembering the siddhis (powers of attainment) in her heart, she called them all and sent them to play host to the king.
bal.306.do306: Hearing Sītā's command, all the siddhis went to where the procession was lodged,
bringing every kind of wealth and comfort, and the pleasures and delights of the city of the gods.
bal.307.cau1: The members of the procession looked at their lodgings and found all the joys of the gods within easy reach in every way.
No one knew anything of the secret of this splendour; all were praising Janaka.
bal.307.cau2: Śrī Rāma knew it was Sītā's glory, and recognising her love he rejoiced at heart.
On hearing of their father's arrival, the two brothers' hearts could not contain their great joy.
bal.307.cau3: Out of diffidence they cannot say it to their guru, yet in their minds is a longing to see their father.
Viśvāmitra saw their great humility, and a special contentment arose in his heart.
bal.307.cau4: Joyfully he held the two brothers to his heart; his body thrilled and his eyes filled with tears.
They went towards the lodging where Daśaratha was, as if a lake had set out with its eyes on the thirsty.
bal.307.do307: The moment King Daśaratha saw the sage coming with his sons,
he rose in joy and went forward, like one feeling for the bottom in an ocean of bliss.
bal.308.cau1: The king prostrated himself before the sage and again and again placed the dust of his feet on his head.
Viśvāmitra drew the king to his heart, blessed him and asked after his welfare.
bal.308.cau2: Then the two brothers prostrated themselves; seeing them, the king could not contain the joy in his heart.
Holding his sons to his heart he wiped away his unbearable sorrow; it was as if a lifeless body had found its life again.
bal.308.cau3: Then they bowed their heads at Vasiṣṭha's feet, and the great sage, glad with love, held them to his heart.
The two brothers paid homage to the assembled Brahmins and received the blessings their hearts desired.
bal.308.cau4: Bharata, with his younger brother Śatrughna, bowed down, and Śrī Rāma raised them and held them to his heart.
Lakṣmaṇa rejoiced to see the two brothers and embraced them, his whole body brimming with love.
bal.308.do308: Townspeople, household, kinsfolk, suppliants, ministers and friends:
the Lord, supremely compassionate and humble, met each of them as was fitting.
bal.309.cau1: Seeing Śrī Rāma, the whole procession was soothed; the ways of that love cannot be told.
Beside the king his four sons shone as if wealth, dharma and the other aims of life had taken bodily form.
bal.309.cau2: Seeing Daśaratha with his sons, the men and women of the city are overjoyed.
The gods shower flowers and beat their drums, and the dancers of heaven dance as they sing.
bal.309.cau3: Śatānanda, and the Brahmins and ministers in their numbers, the bards, the chroniclers, the learned and the heralds:
these welcomers honoured the king together with his procession, then asked leave and went back.
bal.309.cau4: The procession had come before the day fixed for the wedding, so the joy in the city grew all the more.
All the people are tasting the bliss of Brahman, and they ask the Creator to make the days and nights longer.
bal.309.do309: Śrī Rāma and Sītā are the very limit of beauty, and the two kings the limit of merit:
so the townsfolk, men and women gathered in groups, are saying everywhere.
bal.310.cau1: Sītā is Janaka's merit in visible form, and Śrī Rāma is Daśaratha's merit that has taken a body.
No one has worshipped Śiva as these two have, and no one has won a reward to equal theirs.
bal.310.cau2: None like them has been in the world, none is anywhere, and none ever will be.
We too are all a heap of every merit, for we were born into the world as dwellers in Janaka's city.
bal.310.cau3: We have seen the beauty of Jānakī and Śrī Rāma; who is as richly blessed with merit as we are?
And now we shall see Śrī Rāma's wedding and reap in full the reward of having eyes.
bal.310.cau4: The women with voices sweet as the cuckoo's say to one another: Fair-eyed friends, this wedding brings us great gain.
By great good fortune the Creator has brought this about: the two brothers will be guests to our eyes.
bal.310.do310: Moved by affection, Janaka will send for Sītā again and again,
and the two brothers, lovely as ten million Kāmadevas, will come to fetch her.
bal.311.cau1: Then they will be welcomed with hospitality of every kind; who would not love such a home of in-laws, dear?
Each time, all the people of the city will be happy gazing at Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.
bal.311.cau2: Friend, just like the pair of Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, there are two more lads with the king.
One dark, one fair, lovely in every limb: so say all who have been to see them.
bal.311.cau3: One said: I saw them today; it is as if Brahmā had fashioned them with his own hands.
Bharata looks just like Śrī Rāma; men and women cannot tell them apart at a glance.
bal.311.cau4: Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna are alike in form; from toe-nail to crown every limb is peerless.
They delight the heart but cannot be described in words; in all three worlds there is nothing to compare them to.
bal.311.cha1: Tulasīdāsa says: poets and the learned declare that there is nothing anywhere to compare them with.
They are oceans of strength, humility, learning, good character and beauty; none is like them but they themselves.
All the women of the city spread the ends of their saris and speak these words to the Creator:
May all four brothers be wed here in this city, and may we sing the songs of blessing.
bal.311.so311: With tears in their eyes and their bodies thrilling, the women say to one another:
Friend, Śiva, the slayer of Tripura, will bring it all about; both kings are oceans of merit.
bal.312.cau1: In this way all were forming their wishes, their hearts filling with joy that welled up again and again.
The kings who had come to Sītā's svayaṃvara were all made happy too on seeing the brothers.
bal.312.cau2: Telling of Śrī Rāma's bright and boundless fame, the kings went back to their own homes.
Some days passed in this way, with the townsfolk and all the members of the procession full of delight.
bal.312.cau3: The wedding day, the root of all blessings, arrived, in the cold season, in the lovely month of Mārgaśīrṣa.
Planets, lunar day, constellation, yoga and weekday were all excellent; the Creator worked out the auspicious moment and considered it.
bal.312.cau4: He sent through Nārada the very moment that Janaka's astrologers had reckoned.
When everyone heard of this, they said: These astrologers are the Creator himself.
bal.312.do312: It is the pure hour of cow-dust at dusk, the root of every blessing:
so the Brahmins told Janaka, king of Videha, knowing that the omens were favourable.
bal.313.cau1: King Janaka said to his family priest: What reason is there now for delay?
Then Śatānanda called the ministers, and they arrayed all the auspicious things and brought them.
bal.313.cau2: Conches, kettledrums and many tabors sounded, and auspicious pitchers and things of good omen were set out.
Lovely married women sing songs, and holy Brahmins chant the Vedas aloud.
bal.313.cau3: In this way they set out with due honour to fetch the procession, and went to where it was lodged.
Seeing the company of Daśaratha, king of Kosala, they thought even Indra, king of the gods, very small.
bal.313.cau4: They said: The time has come; now be pleased to set out. At these words the kettledrums were struck.
Having asked his guru and performed the family rites, King Daśaratha set out with a company of sages and holy men.
bal.313.do313: Seeing the good fortune and splendour of the king of Avadh, Brahmā and the other gods
began to praise it with a thousand mouths, counting their own births worthless.
bal.314.cau1: The gods knew it for a most auspicious occasion; sounding their drums, they shower flowers.
Śiva, Brahmā and the hosts of the gods mounted their aerial cars in many companies.
bal.314.cau2: Their bodies thrilling with love and their hearts full of zeal, they set out to see Śrī Rāma's wedding.
Seeing Janakapura, the gods were filled with love; to all of them their own worlds seemed small.
bal.314.cau3: Astonished, they gaze at the wonderful canopies; all the work there is of many kinds and beyond this world.
The women and men of the city are treasuries of beauty, graceful, righteous, good-natured and wise.
bal.314.cau4: Seeing them, all the gods and goddesses looked like stars in the light of the moon.
The Creator was especially astonished: nowhere did he see anything of his own making.
bal.314.do314: Śiva counselled all the gods: Do not lose yourselves in wonder.
Be steady and consider in your hearts: this is the wedding of Sītā and Śrī Rāma.
bal.315.cau1: They whose name, taken in the world, destroys the roots of all that is inauspicious,
and puts the four fruits of life in the palm of one's hand — these are that same Sītā and Śrī Rāma, said Śiva.
bal.315.cau2: In this way Śiva counselled the gods, and then drove his fine bull forward.
The gods saw Daśaratha going along, his mind full of great joy and his body thrilling.
bal.315.cau3: With him go the company of saints and the Brahmins, as if joys themselves had taken bodies and were serving him.
Beside him shine his four handsome sons, as if every form of liberation had taken a body.
bal.315.cau4: Seeing the fine pairs, of emerald and of gold in hue, the gods felt no little love.
Then, looking on Śrī Rāma, they rejoiced at heart, and praising the king they showered flowers.
bal.315.do315: Gazing again and again at Śrī Rāma's form, beautiful from toe to crown,
Śiva, and Umā with him, thrilled in every limb, their eyes brimming with tears.
bal.316.cau1: His dark limbs have the sheen of a peacock's throat; his finely coloured garments put lightning to shame.
He is decked in wedding ornaments of many kinds, all auspicious and lovely in every way.
bal.316.cau2: His face is lovely as the spotless autumn moon; his eyes put fresh lotuses to shame.
All that unearthly beauty cannot be told; it delights only within the heart.
bal.316.cau3: His charming brothers shine beside him, making their restless horses prance as they go.
The princes show off their fine horses, and those who sing the line's praises recite its titles of honour.
bal.316.cau4: The horse on which Śrī Rāma is seated — seeing its gait, Garuḍa, king of birds, was ashamed.
It is lovely in every way, beyond telling, as if Kāmadeva had taken the form of a horse.
bal.316.cha1: It is as if Kāmadeva had taken the form of a horse and shone in great splendour for Śrī Rāma's sake,
enchanting all the worlds with his own youth, strength, beauty, virtues and paces.
The jewelled saddle glitters with the light of the fine pearls, gems and rubies set in it;
seeing the lovely bells and the graceful bridle, gods, men and sages were spellbound.
bal.316.do316: Its mind absorbed in the Lord's will, the horse takes on a beauty as it moves,
as though a cloud adorned with stars and lightning were making a fine peacock dance.
bal.317.cau1: Even Sarasvatī cannot describe the fine horse that Śrī Rāma rides.
Śiva, in love with Śrī Rāma's form, found his fifteen eyes exceedingly dear.
bal.317.cau2: When Śrī Hari gazed lovingly at Śrī Rāma, the lord of Ramā, and Ramā with him, were enchanted.
Beholding Śrī Rāma's beauty, the Creator rejoiced, but knowing he had only eight eyes, he regretted it.
bal.317.cau3: Kārttikeya, the commander of the gods, is full of delight at heart: he has the gain of half as many eyes again as the Creator.
Wise Indra gazes at Śrī Rāma and counts Gautama's curse a supreme blessing.
bal.317.cau4: All the gods envy the lord of the gods: today no one is equal to Purandara.
The hosts of gods rejoice to see Śrī Rāma, and in both royal companies the joy is especially great.
bal.317.cha1: Great is the joy in the royal companies on both sides; kettledrums sound loud and many.
The gods shower flowers in delight, crying: Glory, glory, glory to the jewel of Raghu's line!
Thus, as the procession is known to be coming, many instruments play.
The queen calls the married women and prepares the auspicious things for the parichan (the bridegroom's welcome).
bal.317.do317: Decking out lamps for ārati in many ways and arranging all the auspicious things,
the noble women, with the stately gait of elephants, went joyfully to perform the welcome.
bal.318.cau1: All are moon-faced, all doe-eyed; the beauty of each one's form robs Rati of her pride.
They wear fine garments of many colours and have decked their bodies with every ornament.
bal.318.cau2: Their every limb adorned with auspicious things, they sing so that cuckoos are put to shame.
Bracelets, girdle-bells and anklets jingle; seeing their gait, the elephants of Kāmadeva are abashed.
bal.318.cau3: Instruments of many kinds are playing; in the sky and in the city there are auspicious celebrations.
Śacī, Sarasvatī, Lakṣmī, Bhavānī, and all the goddesses who are pure and wise by nature
bal.318.cau4: took on, in disguise, the fair form of women and went and joined the women of the palace.
They sing auspicious songs in sweet voices; all were so overcome with joy that no one knew them.
bal.318.cha1: Who knew whom? Overcome by joy, all went to welcome Brahman, the bridegroom.
Sweet songs, melodious drums, the gods showering flowers: the splendour was lovely to see.
Seeing the bridegroom, the fount of joy, all were glad at heart;
tears welled up in their lotus eyes, and a thrill ran over their lovely limbs.
bal.318.do318: The joy that filled the mind of Sītā's mother at seeing Śrī Rāma in the bridegroom's attire —
that, not even a thousand Sarasvatīs and a thousand Śeṣas could tell in a hundred kalpas.
bal.319.cau1: Knowing the moment auspicious, the queen holds back her tears and performs the welcome with a glad heart.
All the customs laid down in the Vedas and the practice of the family she carried out well.
bal.319.cau2: The five kinds of music sound and auspicious songs are sung; carpets of cloth of many kinds are laid on the way.
After the ārati she offered him arghya, the water of welcome; then Śrī Rāma went on to the pavilion.
bal.319.cau3: Daśaratha took his place in splendour with his company; seeing their grandeur, the guardians of the worlds were put to shame.
From time to time the gods shower flowers, and the Brahmins recite the śānti verses that suit the hour.
bal.319.cau4: In the sky and the city there is such a din that no one can hear anything, his own words or another's.
Thus Śrī Rāma came into the pavilion; they offered him arghya and seated him.
bal.319.cha1: Seating him, performing the ārati and gazing at the bridegroom, they are filled with joy.
The women lavish gems, garments and ornaments in plenty over him and sing auspicious songs.
Brahmā and the other chief gods, disguised as Brahmins, watch the spectacle;
beholding the beauty of Śrī Rāma, the sun to the lotus of Raghu's line, they count their lives fulfilled.
bal.319.do319: The barbers, the bārīs (torchbearers and leaf-plate makers), the bards and the performers, receiving the gifts lavished over Śrī Rāma,
bow their heads and bless him with joy; their hearts cannot hold their delight.
bal.320.cau1: Having performed all the rites of the Veda and of custom, Janaka and Daśaratha met with great love.
The two great kings shone as they met; poets searched and searched for a likeness and were abashed.
bal.320.cau2: Finding none anywhere, they admitted defeat in their hearts and settled on this likeness: these two are like none but themselves.
Seeing the fathers of bride and groom meet, the gods were filled with love; they showered flowers and began to sing their praise.
bal.320.cau3: The gods said: Ever since Brahmā brought forth the world, we have seen and heard of many weddings,
but an array and a company matched in every way, and fathers-in-law so evenly matched, we have seen only today.
bal.320.cau4: At the gods' words, lovely and true, a love beyond this world spread on both sides.
Laying down fine carpets and offering arghya, Janaka respectfully led Daśaratha into the pavilion.
bal.320.cha1: As they looked at the pavilion, its wondrous design and its beauty stole the hearts of the sages.
Wise Janaka brought thrones with his own hands and set them for everyone.
He worshipped Vasiṣṭha as he would the deity of his house, and with humble entreaty received his blessing.
The supreme love with which he worshipped Viśvāmitra is beyond all telling.
bal.320.do320: Joyfully the king worshipped Vāmadeva and the other seers;
to each he gave a divine seat, and from all he received blessings.
bal.321.cau1: Then he worshipped the lord of Kosala, regarding him as equal to God, with no other feeling in his mind.
With folded hands he spoke humbly and in praise, telling how great his own fortune and glory were.
bal.321.cau2: The king worshipped all the members of the wedding party, honouring them in every way as he had his fellow father-in-law.
He gave everyone fitting seats. How can I describe that festivity with one mouth?
bal.321.cau3: Janaka honoured the whole wedding party with gifts, respect, humble entreaty and gracious words.
The Creator, Śrī Hari, Śiva, the guardians of the quarters and the Sun, who know the might of Śrī Rāma,
bal.321.cau4: watch the spectacle in great delight, disguised in the fine dress of Brahmins.
Janaka worshipped them, regarding them as equal to gods, and gave them fine seats without knowing who they were.
bal.321.cha1: Who could recognise, who could know whom? All had lost awareness of themselves.
Seeing the bridegroom, the fount of joy, both sides were filled with joy.
Wise Śrī Rāma knew the gods; he worshipped them in his mind and gave them seats in his mind.
Seeing the Lord's courtesy and nature, the gods were delighted at heart.
bal.321.do321: On the beauty of the moon of Śrī Rāmacandra's face the eyes of all, lovely chakora birds,
drink it in with reverence; their love and delight are not small.
bal.322.cau1: Seeing the hour had come, Vasiṣṭha sent for Śatānanda, who heard and came with respect.
Vasiṣṭha said: Go quickly now and bring the princess. Receiving the command, the sage went gladly.
bal.322.cau2: Hearing the priest's words, the wise queen and her companions were delighted.
She called the Brahmin wives and the elder women of the family, and they performed the family rites and sang auspicious songs.
bal.322.cau3: The fair goddesses who had taken the guise of women were all lovely by nature and in the bloom of youth.
The women are glad to see them; without knowing who they are, they hold them dearer than life.
bal.322.cau4: Again and again the queen honours them, taking them to be like Umā, Ramā and Sarasvatī.
Adorning Sītā and forming a company, they joyfully set out, leading her to the pavilion.
bal.322.cha1: The companions, ladies decked in auspicious finery, went and brought Sītā with respect.
All the fair women had put on the sixteen adornments and moved with the gait of a stately elephant in its pride.
Hearing their sweet singing, sages forsake their meditation, and the cuckoos of Kāmadeva are put to shame.
Anklets, ankle-bells and lovely bracelets ring finely in time with their steps.
bal.322.do322: Sītā, lovely by nature, shines among the company of women
as though Perfect Beauty, in the form of a lovely woman, stood among a host of women who were Beauty itself.
bal.323.cau1: Sītā's beauty cannot be described: the mind is small, and her loveliness is vast.
The wedding guests saw Sītā coming, a store of beauty, holy in every way.
bal.323.cau2: All bowed to her in their hearts; seeing Śrī Rāma, they had every wish fulfilled.
Daśaratha rejoiced with his sons; the joy that filled his heart cannot be told.
bal.323.cau3: The gods bow and rain down flowers; the sages' blessings ring out, the root of all that is auspicious.
Songs and drums make a great uproar; men and women alike are immersed in love and delight.
bal.323.cau4: Thus Sītā came into the pavilion; the great sages, delighted, recite the hymns of peace.
The two family gurus carried out all the rites and customs proper to that occasion.
bal.323.cha1: When the rites are done, the gurus joyfully have Gaurī, Gaṇeśa and the Brahmins worshipped.
The gods appear in person, receive the worship, give their blessings and are deeply pleased.
Whatever madhuparka or other auspicious article the sages wish for in their minds at any moment,
the attendants stand ready with it there and then, filled in golden platters and pitchers.
bal.323.cha2: The Sun told the customs of the family with love, and all was done with reverence.
Having thus had the gods worshipped, they gave Sītā a beautiful throne.
The way Sītā and Śrī Rāma gaze at each other, and their love, no one can perceive;
it is beyond the mind, the intellect and the finest speech: how could a poet bring it to light?
bal.323.do323: At the time of the homa, Agni takes bodily form and accepts the oblations with great joy.
In the guise of Brahmins, all the Vedas tell the rites of the marriage.
bal.324.cau1: Janaka's chief queen, known to all the world, Sītā's mother: how could she be described?
Good fame, merit, happiness and beauty: the Creator gathered them all and fashioned her with care.
bal.324.cau2: Knowing the time had come, the great sages sent for her; at the word, the married women brought her with honour.
Sunayanā shone at Janaka's left, as if Mainā were adorning the side of Himavān.
bal.324.cau3: Fine golden pitchers and jewelled platters, filled with pure, fragrant and auspicious water,
the king and queen joyfully brought with their own hands and set before Śrī Rāma.
bal.324.cau4: The sages recite the Vedas in words of blessing; knowing the moment, the sky pours down flowers.
Seeing the bridegroom, the royal couple were filled with love and began to wash his holy feet.
bal.324.cha1: They began to wash the lotus feet, their bodies thrilling with love.
In the sky and the city, songs, drums and cries of victory seemed to well up and spread in all four directions.
Those lotus feet that ever shine in the lake of the heart of Śiva, the enemy of Kāma,
by remembering which even once the mind becomes pure and all the stains of Kali flee;
bal.324.cha2: by whose touch the sage's wife, who had been laden with sin, attained the highest state;
whose nectar, on Śiva's head, the gods proclaim the very limit of purity;
serving which, with their minds made bees, sages and yogīs reach the state they long for:
those feet the blessed Janaka is washing, and all cry, Glory, glory!
bal.324.cha3: Joining the palms of bridegroom and bride, the two family gurus recite the lineages.
The pāṇigrahaṇa, the taking of the hand, was done; seeing it, the Creator, gods, men and sages are filled with joy.
Seeing the bridegroom, the root of happiness, the couple thrilled in body and their hearts leapt with joy.
Following the ordinances of custom and the Veda, Janaka, the jewel among kings, gave away his daughter.
bal.324.cha4: As Himavān gave Girijā to Śiva, and the Ocean gave Lakṣmī to Śrī Hari,
so Janaka gave Sītā to Śrī Rāma, and a lovely new fame arose in the world.
How could Videha make his entreaty? The dark form had made Videha videha, with no sense of his body left.
The homa was duly performed, the knot was tied, and the rounds began.
bal.324.do324: Cries of victory, the heralds' praises, the chanting of the Vedas, songs of blessing and drums resound;
hearing them, the wise gods rejoice and rain down flowers of the wish-granting tree.
bal.325.cau1: The prince and princess walk the lovely rounds, and all, with reverence, reap the reward of having eyes.
The charming pair is beyond description; whatever likeness I might offer falls short.
bal.325.cau2: The lovely reflections of Śrī Rāma and Sītā glitter in the jewelled pillars,
as if Kāmadeva and Rati had taken many forms to watch Śrī Rāma's peerless wedding.
bal.325.cau3: Their longing to see is great and their shyness no less; they appear and hide again and again.
All who watched were lost in it; like Janaka, they forgot themselves.
bal.325.cau4: The sages joyfully had the rounds walked, and completed every custom along with its gifts.
Śrī Rāma places sindūra on Sītā's head; the beauty of it cannot be told in any way.
bal.325.cau5: It is as if a serpent, greedy for nectar, were adorning the moon with a lotus well filled with red pollen.
Then Vasiṣṭha gave the word, and bridegroom and bride sat on one seat.
bal.325.cha1: Śrī Rāma and Jānakī sat on the seat of honour, and Daśaratha was glad at heart.
Seeing new fruit on the wish-granting tree of his own merit, he thrilled again and again.
Rejoicing filled the worlds; everyone said that Śrī Rāma's wedding had taken place.
How could a single tongue describe this great festivity to its end?
bal.325.cha2: Then, at Vasiṣṭha's bidding, Janaka had the wedding arrangements made ready
and sent for the princesses Māṇḍavī, Śrutakīrti and Ūrmilā.
Kuśaketu's elder daughter, rich in virtue, good conduct, happiness and beauty,
the king, performing every rite with love, gave in marriage to Bharata.
bal.325.cha3: Knowing Jānakī's younger sister to be the crown of all lovely women,
he gave that daughter in marriage to Lakṣmaṇa with every honour.
She whose name was Śrutakīrti, lovely-eyed and fair of face, a treasury of every virtue,
renowned for beauty and good conduct, the king gave to Śatrughna.
bal.325.cha4: The well-matched grooms and brides look at one another and rejoice at heart, though shy.
All, delighted, praise their beauty, and the hosts of gods rain down flowers.
The lovely brides with their handsome grooms all shine in a single pavilion,
as if the four states of the soul, waking and the rest, shone in its heart together with their lords.
bal.325.do325: The lord of Avadh rejoiced to see all his sons with their brides,
as if the jewel among kings had gained the four fruits of life together with the rites that win them.
bal.326.cau1: In the very way that Śrī Rāma's wedding rites were described, all the princes were married.
The vast dowry cannot be told at all; the whole pavilion was filled with gold and gems.
bal.326.cau2: Blankets, garments and wonderful silks, of every kind, in plenty and of no small worth;
elephants, chariots, horses, men and women servants, and cows decked out, like the wish-fulfilling cow.
bal.326.cau3: The gifts were countless: how could one reckon them? They cannot be told; only those who saw them know.
The guardians of the worlds looked on with envy; the lord of Avadh accepted it all gladly.
bal.326.cau4: To those who asked he gave whatever each desired; what was left came to the bridegroom's lodging.
Then Janaka, with folded hands, honouring the whole wedding party, spoke in gentle words.
bal.326.cha1: He honoured the whole wedding party with respect, gifts, humility and praise,
and, full of joy, worshipped the hosts of great sages and bowed to them, lavishing his love on them.
Bowing his head and propitiating the gods, he says to all with folded hands:
Gods and saints want only true feeling; is the ocean satisfied by an offering of a palmful of water?
bal.326.cha2: Then Janaka, with his brother, again joined his hands and spoke to the king of Kosala
in charming words steeped in affection, courtesy and goodness of nature:
O king, through this bond with you we have now become great in every way.
With this kingdom and all its wealth, think of us as your servants, bought without price.
bal.326.cha3: Cherish these girls, taking them as your handmaids, with ever-new kindness.
Forgive my fault in sending for you to come here; I have been very presumptuous.
Then Daśaratha, jewel of the Solar line, heaped every honour on his co-father-in-law.
The courtesies they offered each other cannot be told; their hearts were brimming with love.
bal.326.cha4: Hosts of gods rain down flowers, and the king sets out for his lodging.
With drums, cries of victory and the chanting of the Vedas, there is fine festivity in sky and city.
Then, with the leave of the lord of sages, the lovely companions, singing songs of blessing,
led the bridegrooms with their brides to the bridal chamber (kohabar).
bal.326.do326: Again and again Sītā looks at Śrī Rāma; she is shy, but her heart is not.
Her eyes, thirsting for love, steal the beauty of lovely fish.
bal.327.cau1: Śrī Rāma's dark body is lovely by nature; its beauty puts millions of Kāmadevas to shame.
His lotus feet, tinted with red lac, are lovely; on them the bee-like minds of sages always hover.
bal.327.cau2: His yellow dhoti, holy and charming, steals the brightness of the rising sun and of lightning.
Sweet little bells and a charming cord are at his waist; his long arms bear beautiful ornaments.
bal.327.cau3: The yellow sacred thread adds great splendour; the ring on his hand steals the heart.
He shines, arrayed in all the wedding attire; on his broad chest the chest ornaments gleam.
bal.327.cau4: His yellow scarf is worn across the body, under one arm, with gems and pearls set at both its ends.
His eyes are lotuses, lovely earrings hang at his ears, and his face is the treasury of all beauty.
bal.327.cau5: Lovely brows, a charming nose, and on the forehead a tilaka, the very home of loveliness.
On his head shines the charming bridal crown, strung with auspicious pearls and gems.
bal.327.cha1: Great gems are strung in the lovely crown; every limb steals the heart.
The women of the city and the fair ones of heaven, seeing the bridegroom, all break straws to ward off the evil eye.
Waving gems, clothes and ornaments over him as offerings, they perform ārati and sing songs of blessing.
The gods rain down flowers, and bards, chroniclers and heralds proclaim his fair fame.
bal.327.cha2: The married women, full of joy, brought the princes and princesses into the bridal chamber,
and with great love, singing songs of blessing, began the customary rites.
Gaurī teaches Śrī Rāma the lahakaur, the feeding of morsels to each other, and Sarasvatī tells Sītā.
The queens' household is carried away by the joy of laughter and play; all gain the fruit of their birth.
bal.327.cha3: In the gem on her own hand the image of the treasury of beauty is seen,
and Jānakī does not move her creeper-like arm, for fear of losing the sight of him.
The fun, the play, the delight and the love cannot be told; only her companions know them.
All the lovely companions set out for the lodging, bringing the bridegrooms and the brides.
bal.327.cha4: At that time blessings are heard on every side, and there is great joy in city and sky.
Everyone said with a glad heart: May the four lovely couples live long.
Lords of yogīs, siddhas, great sages and gods, beholding the Lord, beat their drums,
and went rejoicing, each to his own world, raining flowers and crying, Glory, glory, glory!
bal.327.do327: Then all the princes came to their father with their brides,
and it was as if the lodging overflowed, filled with beauty, blessing and joy.
bal.328.cau1: Then a feast of many kinds was made ready, and Janaka sent to invite the wedding guests.
Over peerless cloths spread as a carpet before him, the king went with his sons.
bal.328.cau2: With reverence he washed the feet of all and seated each on a low seat as befitted him.
Janaka washed the feet of the lord of Avadh; his courtesy and affection cannot be described.
bal.328.cau3: Then he washed the lotus feet of Śrī Rāma, which lie hidden in the lotus of Śiva's heart.
Knowing the three brothers to be equal to Śrī Rāma, Janaka washed their feet with his own hands.
bal.328.cau4: The king gave everyone fitting seats and called all the cooks.
With care they began to lay the leaf-plates, made of jewelled leaves pinned with gold.
bal.328.do328: Dal and rice and cow's ghee, fine, tasty and pure,
the skilful, courteous cooks served to everyone in a moment.
bal.329.cau1: Having taken the five ritual morsels, they began to eat, and on hearing the gālī songs, the teasing songs of a wedding, they were filled with delight.
Delicacies of many kinds were laid before them, like nectar, beyond all describing.
bal.329.cau2: The skilled cooks began to serve: dishes of so many kinds that who could know their names?
Food is said to be of four kinds (to chew, to suck, to lick and to drink), and not one of these kinds can be described.
bal.329.cau3: There were fine dishes of many sorts in all six flavours, and of each flavour countless varieties.
As they dine, the gālī songs are sung in sweet voices, naming the men and women one by one.
bal.329.cau4: The teasing, so suited to the hour, was charming; hearing it, King Daśaratha laughs with all his company.
In this way everyone dined, and then water for rinsing the mouth was offered to all with respect.
bal.329.do329: Janaka offered betel and honoured Daśaratha together with his company.
Then Daśaratha, the crown of all kings, went gladly back to the lodging.
bal.330.cau1: In the city there are festivities ever new, and days and nights pass like the blink of an eye.
Very early in the morning the jewel among kings awoke, and the suppliants began to sing the host of his virtues.
bal.330.cau2: Seeing the noble princes together with their brides, how could the joy that filled his heart be told?
Having performed the morning rites, he went to his guru, with great delight and love in his heart.
bal.330.cau3: Bowing, worshipping him and joining his palms, he spoke in words that seemed steeped in nectar:
Listen, king of sages: by your grace, today I have accomplished all I had to do.
bal.330.cau4: Now, master, call all the Brahmins and give them cows adorned in every way.
Hearing this, the guru praised the king, and then sent to summon the company of sages.
bal.330.do330: Vāmadeva, the divine sage Nārada, Vālmīki, Jābāli,
and Viśvāmitra and other ascetics — then a host of the best of sages came.
bal.331.cau1: The king prostrated himself before them all, worshipped them lovingly and gave them seats of honour.
He sent for four lakh fine cows, lovely and gentle in nature like Kāmadhenu, the cow that grants every wish.
bal.331.cau2: Having them all adorned in every way, the king gladly gave them to the Brahmins.
The king makes his humble plea in many ways: Today I have gained the reward of living in the world.
bal.331.cau3: Receiving their blessings, the king rejoiced; then he called the crowds of suppliants.
Gold, clothes, gems, horses, elephants and chariots: Daśaratha, the delight of the Sun's line, gave them, asking each what he wished.
bal.331.cau4: They went away reciting and singing the tale of his virtues: Glory, glory, glory to the lord of the Sun's line!
Such was the festivity of Śrī Rāma's wedding, which even Śeṣa with his thousand mouths could not describe.
bal.331.do331: Bowing his head again and again at Viśvāmitra's feet, the king says:
King of sages, all this happiness is the gift of your gracious glance.
bal.332.cau1: King Daśaratha praises Janaka's affection, courtesy, deeds and splendour in every way.
Each day, on rising, the lord of Avadh asks for leave, and Janaka lovingly keeps him back.
bal.332.cau2: The honour shown grows ever new and greater, and every day the hospitality takes a thousand forms.
In the city there is ever new joy and festivity; Daśaratha's going pleases no one.
bal.332.cau3: Many days passed in this way, as though the wedding party were bound with a rope of love.
Then Viśvāmitra and Śatānanda went and counselled King Janaka, saying:
bal.332.cau4: Now give Daśaratha leave to go, even though you cannot let go of your love.
Saying, Very well, my lords, Janaka sent for his ministers; crying, Victory and long life, they bowed their heads.
bal.332.do332: Janaka said: The lord of Avadh wishes to leave; let it be known within the palace.
Hearing this, ministers, Brahmins, courtiers and the king himself were all overcome with love.
bal.333.cau1: When the townspeople heard that the wedding party was to leave, they asked one another about it in distress.
Hearing that the departure was true, all grew downcast, like lotuses closing at dusk.
bal.333.cau2: Wherever the wedding party had halted on its way to the city, provisions of many kinds were sent.
Dry fruits and delicacies of every sort: that store of food is beyond describing.
bal.333.cau3: Janaka sent many fine things, loaded on countless bullocks and bearers.
He sent a lakh of horses and twenty-five thousand chariots, all adorned from top to toe.
bal.333.cau4: Ten thousand elephants in rut were decked out, at the sight of which the elephants of the quarters felt shamed.
Carriages laden with gold, clothes and gems, and she-buffaloes, cows and goods of every kind were sent.
bal.333.do333: Then Janaka gave besides a boundless dowry that cannot be told,
beside which the wealth of the worlds of the world-guardians looked small.
bal.334.cau1: Having arranged all these things in this way, Janaka sent them on to Ayodhyā.
As soon as they heard the wedding party would leave, all the queens were as distressed as fish in shallow water.
bal.334.cau2: Again and again they take Sītā into their laps, and, blessing her, give her counsel:
May you always be dear to your husband; may your married happiness last long: this is our blessing.
bal.334.cau3: Serve your mother-in-law, your father-in-law and your guru; see your husband's wish and follow his bidding.
The wise companions, moved by deep affection, teach in gentle words a woman's dharma.
bal.334.cau4: The queens counselled all the princesses with care and clasped them to their hearts again and again.
The mothers embrace them over and over and say: Why did Brahmā ever create women?
bal.334.do334: At that time Śrī Rāma, the banner of the Sun's line, with his brothers,
set out gladly for Janaka's palace to take their leave.
bal.335.cau1: The four brothers were lovely by nature, and the men and women of the city ran to see them.
Someone says: They mean to leave today; the king of Videha has made ready for the farewell.
bal.335.cau2: Gaze your fill on the beauty of the king's four sons, our dear guests.
Who knows, wise friend, by what merit of ours the Creator brought them here and made them guests of our eyes?
bal.335.cau3: As nectar to one who must die, as the wish-granting tree of heaven to one hungry from birth,
as the abode of Hari to one who dwells in hell: such for us is the sight of them.
bal.335.cau4: Gaze on Śrī Rāma's beauty and keep it in your heart: make your mind the serpent and his image its jewel.
So, giving all who saw them the reward of their eyes, the princes went into the royal palace.
bal.335.do335: Seeing all the brothers, oceans of beauty, the whole household of the queens rose up in joy.
The mothers-in-law, their hearts full of delight, wave offerings over them and perform ārati.
bal.336.cau1: Seeing Śrī Rāma's beauty they were filled with love, and, overcome by it, they fell at his feet again and again.
No reserve was left; love flooded their hearts. How can such natural affection be told?
bal.336.cau2: They anointed him and his brothers with fragrant paste and bathed them, and with great love fed them food of the six flavours.
Śrī Rāma, seeing that the moment was right, spoke with courtesy, affection and modesty in his words:
bal.336.cau3: The king wishes to set out for Ayodhyā, and he has sent us here to take our leave.
Mother, give us leave with a glad heart, and, knowing us for your children, keep your love for us always.
bal.336.cau4: At these words the queens' household grieved; the mothers-in-law, overcome with love, cannot speak.
They took all the princesses to their hearts, and, entrusting them to their husbands, pleaded with them earnestly.
bal.336.cha1: With humble words the queen gave Sītā over to Śrī Rāma, and, with folded hands, she says again and again:
Dear son, I would give my life for you. You are all-knowing; the state of everyone is known to you.
Know that Sītā is dear as life to her family, to the townspeople, to me and to the king.
Lord of Tulasī, seeing her goodness and her love, regard her as your own handmaid.
bal.336.so336: Every wish of yours stands fulfilled; among the wise you are the crest-jewel, and love is what is dear to you.
Rāma, you take to heart the virtues of your servants, you destroy faults, and you are the home of compassion.
bal.337.cau1: Having said this, the queen stayed clasping his feet, as though her voice had sunk into the mire of love.
Hearing those noble words steeped in affection, Śrī Rāma showed his mother-in-law honour in many ways.
bal.337.cau2: With joined palms Śrī Rāma asked for leave and bowed to her again and again.
Receiving her blessing and bowing his head once more, Śrī Rāma set out with his brothers.
bal.337.cau3: Bringing his lovely, sweet form into their hearts, all the queens grew faint with love.
Then, gathering courage, they called the princesses, and the mothers embrace them again and again.
bal.337.cau4: They go a little way with them, then turn and embrace them once more; the love between them grew, and not a little.
As they met again and again, the companions drew them apart, as a cow that has just calved is drawn from her young calf.
bal.337.do337: All the men and women, and the queens' household with the companions, were overcome with love,
as if Compassion and Separation had taken up their dwelling in the city of Videha.
bal.338.cau1: The parrots and mynas that Jānakī had reared, and kept in golden cages and taught to speak,
cry out in distress: Where is Vaidehī? Who, hearing them, would not lose all composure?
bal.338.cau2: When birds and beasts were so distressed, how could the state of human beings be told?
Then Janaka came with his brother; love welled up in him and his eyes filled with tears.
bal.338.cau3: At the sight of Sītā his composure fled, he who was called supremely dispassionate.
The king clasped Jānakī to his heart, and the great bounds of knowledge gave way.
bal.338.cau4: All his wise ministers counsel him; then he reflected, and knew that this was not the moment for it.
Again and again he clasped his daughters to his heart, and sent for fine palanquins, richly decked.
bal.338.do338: The whole family was overcome with love; the king, knowing the auspicious hour had come,
called Siddhi and Gaṇeśa to mind and seated the princesses in the palanquins.
bal.339.cau1: In many ways the king counselled his daughters, and taught them a wife's dharma and the customs of the family.
He gave many maidservants and menservants, pure-hearted attendants who were dear to Sītā.
bal.339.cau2: As Sītā leaves, the people of the city are distraught, and fair omens appear, heaps of blessing.
With the Brahmins, the ministers and all his company, the king went along to see them on their way.
bal.339.cau3: Seeing that the hour had come, the instruments struck up, and the wedding guests made ready chariots, elephants and horses.
Daśaratha summoned all the Brahmins and filled them full with gifts and honour.
bal.339.cau4: With the dust of their lotus feet set upon his head, and their blessing received, the king was glad.
Remembering Gaṇeśa, he set out, and many omens appeared, the roots of all blessing.
bal.339.do339: The gods joyfully rain down flowers and the apsarās sing.
The lord of Avadh set out gladly for the city of Avadh, to the beat of kettledrums.
bal.340.cau1: With courteous entreaty the king sent back the leading citizens, and respectfully called all who had come to ask for gifts.
He gave them ornaments, clothes, horses and elephants, and, nourishing them with love, set them all on their feet.
bal.340.cau2: Singing his praises again and again, they all turned back, keeping Śrī Rāma in their hearts.
Again and again the king of Kosala asks him to turn back, but Janaka, held by love, does not wish to return.
bal.340.cau3: Then Daśaratha spoke gracious words once more: Turn back now, O king; you have come a long way.
Then the king got down from his chariot and stood, and a flood of loving tears welled in his eyes.
bal.340.cau4: Then Janaka, king of Videha, spoke with joined hands, in words that seemed steeped in the nectar of love:
In what way shall I frame my humble prayer? Great king, you have exalted me.
bal.340.do340: The lord of Kosala honoured his co-father-in-law and his kinsmen in every way.
They met each other with great humility, and their love would not be held within their hearts.
bal.341.cau1: Janaka bowed his head to the company of sages and received the blessing of every one.
Then with reverence he embraced his sons-in-law, all the brothers, treasuries of beauty, goodness and virtue.
bal.341.cau2: Joining his lovely lotus hands, he spoke words that seemed born of love itself:
Rāma, how shall I praise you? You are the swan of the Mānasa lake that is the mind of the sages and of Śiva.
bal.341.cau3: He for whose sake yogīs practise yoga, giving up anger, delusion, attachment and pride;
the all-pervading Brahman, unseen and imperishable, consciousness and bliss, beyond all attributes and a store of every virtue;
bal.341.cau4: whom speech, together with the mind, does not know, and whom none who reason by inference can reach by argument;
whose greatness the Veda tells by saying neti, not this; who remains the same through the three times:
bal.341.do341: he who is the root of all happiness has come before my eyes.
When God is favourable, every gain in the world comes to a living being.
bal.342.cau1: In every way you have given me honour; knowing me for your own, you have made me yours.
Were there ten thousand Sarasvatīs and Śeṣas, and were they to keep count for millions of kalpas,
bal.342.cau2: the tale of my good fortune and of your virtues would still not be told to its end; hear me, O Lord of the Raghus.
What I say, I say on the strength of one thing alone: you are won by even a very little love.
bal.342.cau3: Again and again, with joined hands, I ask this: may my mind never leave your feet, even by mistake.
Hearing these noble words, as though nourished by love, Śrī Rāma, whose every desire is fulfilled, was well pleased.
bal.342.cau4: With noble, humble words he honoured his father-in-law, and held him equal to his father, to Viśvāmitra and to Vasiṣṭha.
Then Janaka made his humble request to Bharata, and embracing him lovingly gave him his blessing.
bal.342.do342: The king met Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna and gave them his blessing.
Overcome by love for one another, they bow their heads again and again.
bal.343.cau1: With humble words and praise again and again, Śrī Rāma set out with all his brothers.
Janaka went and clasped Viśvāmitra's feet, and touched the dust of his feet to his head and eyes.
bal.343.cau2: Janaka said: Hear me, lord of sages. Through the precious sight of you nothing is beyond reach; this is the faith of my heart.
The happiness and fair fame that the guardians of the worlds desire, yet shrink even from wishing for,
bal.343.cau3: that happiness and fame, my lord, have come easily to me; all attainments follow in the wake of your sight.
Bowing his head again and again he made his humble request, and receiving the blessing the king turned back.
bal.343.cau4: The procession set out to the beat of kettledrums; the whole company, small and great, was glad.
The men and women of the villages, seeing Śrī Rāma, gain the reward of their eyes and are made happy.
bal.343.do343: Halting at fine places along the way and giving joy to the people on the road,
the wedding procession arrived near Avadh on a holy day.
bal.344.cau1: Kettledrums were struck and fine tabors sounded; bherīs and conches rang out, horses neighed and elephants trumpeted.
Cymbals, the birava and the lovely ḍiṇḍimī drum sounded, and shehnāīs play in sweet rāgas.
bal.344.cau2: Hearing that the procession was coming, all the people of the city were glad, their bodies thrilling with joy.
Each adorned his own fine house, and the markets, roads, crossroads and city gates.
bal.344.cau3: All the lanes were sprinkled with argajā perfume, and here and there lovely squares were drawn on the ground.
The market was decked beyond description, with arches, flags, pennants and canopies.
bal.344.cau4: Areca palms, plantains and mangoes laden with fruit were planted, and bakula, kadamba and tamāla trees.
The lovely trees set there reach down to touch the ground; their basins are of gems, finely worked.
bal.344.do344: In house after house auspicious pitchers of many kinds were made and adorned.
Brahmā and all the gods, seeing the city of Śrī Rāma, look on it with longing.
bal.345.cau1: At that time the king's palace shone so that, seeing its design, Kāmadeva's mind was charmed.
Auspiciousness, good omens, charm, prosperity, success, happiness and lovely wealth:
bal.345.cau2: all these festal joys, lovely by nature, seemed each to have taken bodily form and filled the house of Daśaratha.
Tell me, who would not long to see Śrī Rāma and Vaidehī?
bal.345.cau3: In band upon band the married women set out together, their beauty putting to shame Rati, the consort of Kāmadeva.
All of them, with every auspicious thing and their lamps for ārati made ready, sing, as if Sarasvatī herself sang in many forms.
bal.345.cau4: There is a joyful clamour in the king's palace; that time and that joy cannot be described.
Kausalyā and the other mothers of Śrī Rāma, overcome by love, forgot all thought of their bodies.
bal.345.do345: Having worshipped Gaṇeśa and Śiva, they gave Brahmins gifts in plenty.
They were overjoyed, like one utterly poor who has gained the four fruits of life.
bal.346.cau1: All the mothers are overcome with joy upon joy; their feet will not move, their bodies have gone limp.
Filled with longing love for the sight of Śrī Rāma, they all began to arrange the things for the parichan, the welcome rite.
bal.346.cau2: Instruments of many kinds sounded, and Sumitrā gladly arranged the auspicious things:
turmeric, dūb grass, curd, fresh leaves, flowers, betel and areca nut, the very roots of blessing;
bal.346.cau3: unbroken rice, sprouts, gorocana, parched rice and lovely sprigs of tulasī shine there.
Painted golden pitchers, lovely by nature, look as if Kāmadeva's birds had built their nests.
bal.346.cau4: The auspicious things and the perfumes cannot be described; all the queens are arranging every auspicious thing.
They prepared lamps for ārati in many ways, and gladly sing sweet songs of blessing.
bal.346.do346: Filling golden platters with auspicious things and holding them in their lotus hands,
the mothers went gladly to perform the welcome, their bodies thrilling like a tree breaking into leaf.
bal.347.cau1: The smoke of incense darkened the sky, as though the clouds of Sāvan were massing.
The gods rain garlands of flowers from the wish-granting tree, like rows of cranes that draw the mind.
bal.347.cau2: The lovely jewelled festoons look as though Indra had arrayed his bows across the sky.
Fair women appear and vanish on the terraces, like lovely restless flashes of lightning.
bal.347.cau3: The sound of kettledrums is the clouds' deep thunder; those who ask for gifts are the cātaka birds, the frogs and the peacocks.
The gods rain pure, fragrant water, and all the men and women of the city are happy like the crops.
bal.347.cau4: Knowing the hour, the guru gave his command, and King Daśaratha, the jewel of Raghu's line, entered the city:
the king, glad at heart, with all his company, remembering Śiva, Pārvatī and Gaṇeśa.
bal.347.do347: Omens appear; the gods beat their kettledrums and rain down flowers.
The women of the gods dance with joy, singing sweet songs of blessing.
bal.348.cau1: Chroniclers, bards, heralds and skilled players sing the glory renowned through the three worlds.
Cries of victory and the pure, noble chant of the Vedas, steeped in blessing, are heard in all ten directions.
bal.348.cau2: Many instruments began to play; the gods in the sky and the people in the city were filled with love.
The wedding guests in their finery are beyond description; their hearts are full of joy, more than they can hold.
bal.348.cau3: Then the citizens greeted the king with reverence, and at the sight of Śrī Rāma they were filled with happiness.
They wave gems and garments over him as offerings; tears fill their eyes and their bodies thrill.
bal.348.cau4: The women of the city gladly perform ārati, and rejoice to see the four fair princes.
Lifting the curtains of the lovely palanquins, they see the brides and are made happy.
bal.348.do348: Thus, giving joy to all, they came to the palace gate.
The mothers joyfully perform the welcome rite for the princes and their brides.
bal.349.cau1: They wave the lamps again and again; who could tell the bounds of their love and delight?
Ornaments, gems and garments of many kinds they lavish as offerings in countless ways.
bal.349.cau2: Seeing the four sons with their brides, the mothers were lost in supreme bliss.
Gazing again and again on the beauty of Sītā and Śrī Rāma, they rejoice and count their life in the world fulfilled.
bal.349.cau3: Sītā's companions gaze at her face again and again and sing, praising their own good merit.
Moment after moment the gods shower flowers; they dance, they sing and they offer their service.
bal.349.cau4: Seeing the four charming couples, Sarasvatī searched through every comparison;
none would serve, all seemed far too slight, and she stayed gazing unblinking, enraptured by their beauty.
bal.349.do349: Following the way of the Vedas and the custom of the family, offering arghya and spreading cloths along the path,
the mothers performed the welcoming rite for all the sons with their brides and led them into the palace.
bal.350.cau1: There were four thrones, lovely by their very nature, as if Kāmadeva had made them with his own hands.
On them they seated the princesses and the princes, and reverently washed their holy feet.
bal.350.cau2: With incense, lamps and offerings of food, by the rite of the Vedas, they worshipped the bridegrooms and brides, treasuries of all that is auspicious.
Again and again they wave the lamps, and lovely fans and fly-whisks sway over their heads.
bal.350.cau3: Many things are lavished as offerings; brimming with delight, all the mothers look as radiant
as a yogī who has found the supreme reality, as one sick all his life who has received nectar,
bal.350.cau4: as a pauper from birth who has found the philosopher's stone, as a blind man granted the blessing of eyes,
as a mute whose mouth Sarasvatī has come to fill, and as a hero who has won victory in battle.
bal.350.do350क: The mothers feel a joy a thousand million times greater than these joys,
for Śrī Rāma, the moon of Raghu's line, has come home married, with his brothers.
bal.350.do350ख: The mothers perform the customs of the world, and the bridegrooms and brides are shy.
Seeing all this great joy and merriment, Śrī Rāma smiles to himself.
bal.351.cau1: They worshipped the gods and the ancestors with due rites, and every wish of their hearts was fulfilled.
Bowing to all, they ask this boon of them: that all may be well with Śrī Rāma and his brothers.
bal.351.cau2: Unseen, the gods give their blessings, and the mothers gladly gather them, filling the ends of their saris.
The king sent for the members of the wedding party and gave them carriages, garments, gems and ornaments.
bal.351.cau3: Given leave by the king, with Śrī Rāma kept in their hearts, all went gladly to their own homes.
The king had every man and woman of the city clothed in new garments, and in house after house the music of rejoicing began to play.
bal.351.cau4: Whatever the seekers of alms ask for, the king joyfully gives them that very thing.
All the servants and the musicians of many kinds he filled to the full with gifts and honour.
bal.351.do351: All salute him, give their blessings and sing the tale of his many virtues.
Then the lord of men went into the palace with the guru and the Brahmins.
bal.352.cau1: Whatever Vasiṣṭha commanded, the king reverently carried out by the rule of the world and of the Vedas.
Seeing the throng of Brahmins, all the queens rose reverently, counting it their great good fortune.
bal.352.cau2: Their feet were washed and all were bathed, and the king worshipped them well and fed them.
Richly sustained with honour, gifts and love, they went their way content at heart, giving their blessings.
bal.352.cau3: The king worshipped Viśvāmitra, son of Gādhi, in many ways and said: My lord, there is no one else as blessed as I.
The king praised him greatly and, with the queens, took the dust of his feet.
bal.352.cau4: He gave the sage a fine lodging within the palace, and the king and the queens stayed watchful of his every wish.
Then the king worshipped the guru's lotus feet and made his entreaty, with no little love in his heart.
bal.352.do352: All the princes and their brides, and the king and his queens,
bow again and again at the guru's feet, and the lord of sages gives his blessing.
bal.353.cau1: With the deepest love in his heart the king made his entreaty, setting his sons and all his wealth before him.
The chief of sages asked for his customary gift and took it, and blessed him in many ways.
bal.353.cau2: Holding Śrī Rāma with Sītā in his heart, the guru went gladly to his dwelling.
The king sent for all the Brahmins' wives and clothed them in fine garments and ornaments.
bal.353.cau3: Then he sent for the married women whose husbands lived and gave them robes, judging what each would like.
Those entitled to customary gifts all take their due, and the jewel among kings gives as each desires.
bal.353.cau4: The guests he knew to be dear and worthy of honour, the king honoured well.
The gods, having seen Śrī Rāma's wedding, showered flowers and praised the festivity,
bal.353.do353: and, beating their drums, went happily each to his own realm,
telling one another of Śrī Rāma's glory, their hearts unable to hold their love.
bal.354.cau1: Having honoured everyone in every way and sent them off, the king, his heart brimming with joy,
went to where the queens' apartments were, and beheld the princes with their brides.
bal.354.cau2: He took them joyfully on his lap; who could tell how great the happiness was?
He lovingly seated the brides on his lap and, glad at heart, caressed them again and again.
bal.354.cau3: Seeing this gathering, the women of the palace rejoiced, and joy made its home in every heart.
The king told how the wedding had taken place, and as they heard it all were filled with gladness.
bal.354.cau4: King Janaka's virtues, his character and greatness, the way of his love and his splendid wealth,
the king described in many ways, as a bard would; hearing of his deeds, all the queens were overjoyed.
bal.354.do354: The king bathed with his sons, sent for the Brahmins, the guru and his kinsmen,
and dined on many kinds of dishes; by then five ghaṛīs of the night had passed.
bal.355.cau1: Lovely women sing auspicious songs, and the night became enchanting, a very root of joy.
After rinsing their mouths all were given betel, and adorned with garlands and perfumes they were full of beauty.
bal.355.cau2: Having looked on Śrī Rāma and received the king's leave, all bowed their heads and went to their own homes.
The love, the delight, the merriment and the grandeur, the hour, the gathering and its charm
bal.355.cau3: not even a hundred Sarasvatīs and Śeṣas, the Vedas, Brahmā, Maheśa and Gaṇeśa could tell.
How then shall I describe it? Can an earthworm bear the earth upon its head?
bal.355.cau4: The king honoured everyone in every way, and with gentle words called the queens.
He said: The brides are young girls and have come to another's home; keep them as the eyelids keep the eyes.
bal.355.do355: The boys are tired and overcome with sleep; go and put them to bed.
So saying, the king went to his chamber of rest, his mind fixed on the feet of Śrī Rāma.
bal.356.cau1: Hearing the king's words, pleasing by their very nature, the queens had golden beds set with gems made ready.
On them were spread many lovely, soft and graceful sheets, like the foam of cow's milk.
bal.356.cau2: The fine pillows are beyond description; the jewelled chamber held garlands and perfumes.
There were lamps of jewels and a most beautiful canopy; it cannot be put into words: only one who has seen it knows.
bal.356.cau3: Having made a lovely bed, the mothers raised Śrī Rāma and lovingly laid him down on it.
Śrī Rāma bade his brothers again and again, and they too lay down to sleep, each on his own bed.
bal.356.cau4: Seeing Śrī Rāma's dark, tender and lovely limbs, all the mothers speak to him with love:
Dear son, on your way, how did you slay Tāṛakā, so fearsome and so huge?
bal.356.do356: Those dreadful demons, formidable warriors who in battle counted no one as anything —
how did you slay the wicked Mārīca and Subāhu, together with their helpers?
bal.357.cau1: Dear son, may I be a sacrifice for you; by the sage's grace God turned aside many dangers.
You two brothers guarded the sacrifice and, by the guru's grace, gained all knowledge.
bal.357.cau2: At the touch of the dust of your feet the sage's wife was saved, and your fame has filled the worlds.
Śiva's bow, hard as the tortoise's back, the thunderbolt and a mountain peak, you broke in the assembly of kings.
bal.357.cau3: You won the glory of conquering the world, and won Jānakī, and all you brothers have come home married.
All your deeds beyond human power were brought to pass by Kauśika's grace alone.
bal.357.cau4: Dear son, seeing your moon-like face today, our birth in this world has borne fruit.
May Brahmā not reckon in our count the days that passed without our seeing you.
bal.357.do357: With humble and gracious words Śrī Rāma set all the mothers' hearts at rest.
Then, remembering the feet of Śiva, the guru and the Brahmins, he let his eyes yield to sleep.
bal.358.cau1: Even in sleep his face looks most lovely, like a lotus folding into sleep at dusk.
In house after house the women keep the night's vigil and sing to one another the auspicious teasing songs of a wedding.
bal.358.cau2: The queens say: Look, friend, the city is resplendent and the night is radiant.
The mothers-in-law went to sleep holding the lovely brides close, as serpents hide their crest-jewels in their breasts.
bal.358.cau3: At the holy hour of dawn the Lord awoke, and the fine cocks began to crow.
Bards and minstrels sang his many virtues, and the townspeople came to the door to pay their respects.
bal.358.cau4: Bowing to the Brahmins, the gods, the guru, their father and their mothers, and receiving their blessings, all the brothers were glad.
The mothers gazed fondly on their faces, and they went out to the door with the king.
bal.358.do358: Pure by their very nature, the brothers all performed their ablutions and bathed in the holy river,
and, having done their morning rites, the four brothers came to their father.
bal.359.cau1: Seeing them, the king held them to his heart; at his bidding they sat down, rejoicing.
Seeing Śrī Rāma, the whole assembly was content, deeming this the utmost that eyes could gain.
bal.359.cau2: Then the sages Vasiṣṭha and Viśvāmitra came, and the king seated them on fine seats.
With his sons he worshipped them and bowed at their feet; gazing at Śrī Rāma, both gurus were filled with love.
bal.359.cau3: Vasiṣṭha tells sacred histories of dharma, and the king listens with the queens of the palace.
The deeds of Viśvāmitra, son of Gādhi, beyond the reach even of sages' minds, Vasiṣṭha gladly described in many ways.
bal.359.cau4: Vāmadeva said: All of this is true; the sage's fair fame has spread through the three worlds.
Hearing this, everyone rejoiced; in the hearts of Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa the delight was greater still.
bal.359.do359: Every day brings auspicious rites, joy and festivity, and so the days go by.
Brimming with joy, Ayodhyā overflowed, swelling more and more.
bal.360.cau1: An auspicious day was chosen and the lovely wedding wristlets were untied; auspicious rites, joy and merriment were plentiful.
Seeing the ever-new happiness, the gods look on with longing and beg the Creator for birth in Ayodhyā.
bal.360.cau2: Viśvāmitra wishes each day to leave, but stays, held by Śrī Rāma's loving entreaty.
Day by day the king's devotion grows a hundredfold; seeing it, the great sage praises it.
bal.360.cau3: When the sage asked leave, the king was overcome with love and stood before him with his sons.
He said: My lord, all this wealth is yours; I, with my sons and wives, am your servant.
bal.360.cau4: Always hold the boys in your affection, and keep granting me too the sight of you, O sage.
Saying this, the king fell at his feet with his sons and queens; no words would come from his mouth.
bal.360.cau5: Viśvāmitra, the Brahmin, gave his blessings in many ways and set out; the ways of love cannot be told.
Śrī Rāma, with all his brothers, lovingly went with him to see him off, and returned when he gave them leave.
bal.360.do360: Śrī Rāma's beauty, the king's devotion, the wedding, the festivities and the joy:
praising all these inwardly, Viśvāmitra, the moon of Gādhi's line, goes on his way, delighted.
bal.361.cau1: Vāmadeva and Vasiṣṭha, the wise guru of the Raghu line, told the story of Gādhi's son once more.
Hearing the sage's fair fame, the king began to recount inwardly the power of his own merit.
bal.361.cau2: The people went back once the king had given the command, and the king went into the palace with his sons.
Everywhere all sang of Śrī Rāma's wedding; his holy fame spread over the three worlds.
bal.361.cau3: Since Śrī Rāma came home married, joy has dwelt in all Ayodhyā.
Such festivity as there was at the Lord's wedding neither Sarasvatī nor Śeṣa, lord of serpents, can describe.
bal.361.cau4: Knowing the glory of Śrī Rāma and Sītā to be the life of the line of poets, purifying and a mine of blessings,
I have therefore told something of it, to make my own speech holy.
bal.361.cha1: To make his own speech pure, Tulasīdāsa has told the glory of Śrī Rāma.
The story of Śrī Rāma is a boundless ocean: what poet has ever reached its farther shore?
Those who hear of the joyful, auspicious festivities of the sacred thread and the wedding and sing of them with reverence
ever find happiness by the grace of Vaidehī and Śrī Rāma.
bal.361.so361: Those who lovingly sing and hear of the wedding of Sītā and Śrī Rāma
know rejoicing always; the glory of Śrī Rāma is the home of all blessings.
ayodhya.0.shloka1: He in whose lap the daughter of the mountain shines, on whose head the river of the gods,
on whose forehead the young moon, in whose throat the poison, and on whose chest the king of serpents;
he who is adorned with ash, the foremost of the gods, the ruler of all,
Śarva, all-pervading, Śiva, fair as the moon: may that Śrī Śaṅkara protect me always.
ayodhya.0.shloka2: That which neither brightened at the coronation nor faded at the sorrow of exile in the forest,
the beauty of Śrī Rāma's lotus face: may it ever bring me lovely blessings.
ayodhya.0.shloka3: Dark and soft of limb as the blue lotus, with Sītā seated at his left side,
a mighty arrow and a lovely bow in hand: to Rāma, the lord of Raghu's line, I bow.
ayodhya.0.dou1: Making the mirror of my own mind clean with dust from my revered Guru's lotus feet,
I tell the spotless glory of Śrī Rāma, which grants the four fruits of life (dharma, wealth, desire and liberation).
ayodhya.1.cau1: Ever since Śrī Rāma came home married, there have been fresh festivities, joy and rejoicing every day.
On the fourteen worlds, as on great mountains, the clouds of merit pour down the rain of happiness.
ayodhya.1.cau2: Lovely rivers of prosperity, success and wealth swelled and came flowing into the ocean of Avadh.
The men and women of the city are clusters of gems of the finest kind, pure, priceless and beautiful in every way.
ayodhya.1.cau3: The splendour of the city cannot be told at all; it is as if Brahmā's craft had gone this far and no further.
All the people of the city are content in every way, for they behold the moon of Śrī Rāma's face.
ayodhya.1.cau4: The mothers, with all their friends and companions, are glad: they see the vine of their hopes in fruit.
Seeing and hearing of Śrī Rāma's beauty, virtues, gentleness and nature, the king is overjoyed.
ayodhya.1.do1: All have this one wish at heart, and praying to Śiva they say:
May the king, in his own lifetime, give Śrī Rāma the place of crown prince.
ayodhya.2.cau1: Once the king of the Raghus sat in state in the royal court with all his assembly.
The king, the embodiment of all merit, was full of delight at hearing of Śrī Rāma's fair fame.
ayodhya.2.cau2: All kings live in hope of his favour, and the guardians of the worlds keep to his wishes and show him love.
In the three worlds and the three times, nowhere in creation is anyone as fortunate as Daśaratha.
ayodhya.2.cau3: Whatever is said of one whose son is Śrī Rāma, the root of all blessings, falls short.
The king happened to take a mirror in hand, and as he looked at his face he put his crown level.
ayodhya.2.cau4: Near his ears the hair had turned white, as if old age were giving him this counsel:
O king, make Śrī Rāma crown prince; why not take the reward of your life and your birth?
ayodhya.2.do2: With this thought taken to heart, the king found an auspicious day and a fitting moment,
and, his body thrilling with love and his mind glad, he went and told it to his guru.
ayodhya.3.cau1: The king said: Hear me, O lord of sages. Rāma has become capable of all things in every respect.
Servants, ministers, all the citizens, and those who are our enemies, our friends or neither,
ayodhya.3.cau2: to all of them Rāma is dear, just as he is to me; he is your blessing, as it were, shining in bodily form.
Lord, every Brahmin and his household are as fond of him as you are.
ayodhya.3.cau3: Whoever bears the dust of the guru's feet on his head has, it seems, every kind of wealth at his command.
Nobody has tasted this truth as I have, for every good thing came to me from honouring that pure dust.
ayodhya.3.cau4: One longing is in my mind now; your favour, my lord, will bring it to pass.
The sage's heart warmed at the king's natural affection, and he said: Give the order, O king.
ayodhya.3.do3: O king, your name and fame alone grant every wish.
O jewel among kings, the desire of your heart only follows after its fruit.
ayodhya.4.cau1: Knowing in his heart that the guru was pleased in every way, the king spoke gently and with joy:
My lord, let Rāma be made crown prince. Be gracious and say the word, and let the preparations be made.
ayodhya.4.cau2: While I am still here, let this joyful event happen, and let every eye among the people be rewarded.
Śiva, by your favour, my lord, has carried all my affairs through; this single longing is what my heart holds.
ayodhya.4.cau3: Then it will not trouble me whether this body lasts or falls; only let nothing be left for me to regret.
The sage heard Daśaratha's pleasing words, and they, the root of blessing and joy, delighted his heart.
