lanka.98.cha1: The fierce blow of the kick to his chest left Rāvaṇa reeling, and he fell from his chariot to the earth.
He was clutching bears in all twenty hands, like bees lodged in lotuses at night.
Finding him senseless, the king of the bears kicked him once more and went to the Lord.
Knowing that night had come, the charioteer laid him in the chariot and set about bringing him round.
lanka.98.do98: Their swoon over, all the bears and monkeys came to the Lord.
All the demons, in great dread, stayed gathered round Rāvaṇa.
lanka.99.cau1: That very night Trijaṭā went to Sītā and told her all that had happened.
When Sītā heard how the enemy's heads and arms kept growing, a great fear filled her heart.
lanka.99.cau2: Her face clouded and anxiety rose in her mind; then Sītā said to Trijaṭā:
Mother, why do you not tell me what will happen? How is he to die, this tormentor of the world?
lanka.99.cau3: Even with his heads cut off by Śrī Rāma's arrows he does not die; Fate is turning everything the wrong way.
What keeps him alive is my ill fortune, which tore me from Śrī Hari's lotus feet.
lanka.99.cau4: The Fate that conjured the false golden deer of deceit is still angry with me;
the Fate that made me bear unbearable sorrow and made me speak bitter words to Lakṣmaṇa,
lanka.99.cau5: that has taken aim again and again and struck me with the heavy, poisoned arrows of separation from Śrī Rāma,
and that keeps me alive even in such sorrow: that same Fate keeps him alive, and no other.
lanka.99.cau6: Jānakī laments in many ways, recalling again and again the treasury of compassion.
Trijaṭā said: Hear me, princess. Let an arrow strike the gods' enemy in the heart, and he dies.
lanka.99.cau7: But the Lord does not strike him in the heart, because you, Vaidehī, dwell in his heart.
lanka.99.cha1: The Lord reasons: Jānakī dwells in his heart, and in Jānakī's heart is my dwelling;
in my belly are many worlds, and once the arrow strikes, all of them will perish.
Hearing this, Sītā felt great joy and great sorrow at once; seeing it, Trijaṭā spoke again:
Listen, fair one, this is how the enemy will now die; put away your great doubt.
lanka.99.do99: As his heads are cut off he will grow frantic, and his mind will lose its hold on you.
Then Śrī Rāma, who knows all, will strike Rāvaṇa in the heart.
lanka.100.cau1: With these words, after comforting her in many ways, Trijaṭā went back to her own house.
Remembering Śrī Rāma's nature, Vaidehī was seized by the bitter pain of separation.
lanka.100.cau2: She finds fault with the night and with the moon in many ways: the night has become as long as an age and does not pass.
Grieving in separation from Śrī Rāma, Jānakī weeps bitterly within her heart.
lanka.100.cau3: When the burning of separation in her heart grew unbearable, her left eye and arm throbbed.
She read it as a good omen and grew calm within: now the compassionate Śrī Rāma will come to me.
lanka.100.cau4: Meanwhile, at midnight, Rāvaṇa woke and began to rage at his charioteer:
Fool, you took me away from the battlefield! Shame, shame on you, you base, dull-witted wretch!
lanka.100.cau5: Holding his feet, the charioteer talked him round in many ways; at daybreak Rāvaṇa mounted his chariot and charged again.
When they heard that the ten-headed one was coming, a great commotion broke out in the monkey host.
lanka.100.cau6: The great warriors uprooted mountains and trees on every side and charged, grinding their teeth.
lanka.100.cha1: Fearsome monkeys and dreadful bears rushed in, gripping mountains.
They strike in towering rage, and under their blows the demons fled.
The strong monkeys broke the demon host and then hemmed Rāvaṇa in again.
From all four sides they slapped him and tore at his body with their nails, until he was in agony.
lanka.100.do100: Seeing how mighty the monkeys were, Rāvaṇa thought it over,
and vanishing in the twinkling of an eye, he spread out his illusion far and wide.
lanka.101.cha1: When he worked this deceit, fierce creatures appeared:
vampires, ghosts and ghouls, holding bows and iron arrows in their hands.
lanka.101.cha2: Yoginīs grip swords, and in one hand they hold human skulls.
Drinking fresh blood, they dance and sing many songs.
lanka.101.cha3: They raise a terrible cry of Seize! Kill!, and the sound fills every quarter.
They rush with gaping mouths to devour; then the monkeys began to flee.
lanka.101.cha4: Wherever the monkeys run, they see fire burning there.
The monkeys and bears were distraught; then sand began to rain down.
lanka.101.cha5: Leaving the monkeys stunned and helpless here and there, Rāvaṇa roared again.
All the warriors, Lakṣmaṇa and Sugrīva, king of the monkeys, among them, fell senseless.
lanka.101.cha6: Crying Alas, Rāma! Alas, Lord of the Raghus!, the great warriors wring their hands.
Having thus broken the strength of all, he worked another deceit.
lanka.101.cha7: He made many Hanumāns appear, who rushed forward holding rocks.
Forming hosts on every side, they went and surrounded Śrī Rāma.
lanka.101.cha8: Kill him! Seize him! Do not let him go! they cry, gnashing their teeth with tails raised.
Tails gleam in all ten directions, and in their midst stands the king of Kosala.
lanka.101.cha1_2: In their midst the beautiful dark body of the king of Kosala shone with such splendour
as if many rainbows had made a fine hedge round a tall tamāla tree.
Seeing the Lord so, the gods felt joy and grief at once in their hearts and cried: Victory, victory, victory!
Then Śrī Rāma, in anger, dispelled the illusion with a single arrow in the twinkling of an eye.
lanka.101.cha2_2: The illusion gone, the monkeys and bears were glad, and every one of them turned back with trees and mountains in hand.
Śrī Rāma loosed a multitude of arrows, and Rāvaṇa's arms and heads fell to the ground once more.
Those who might sing of the deeds of the battle between Śrī Rāma and Rāvaṇa for many aeons,
though they were hundreds of Śeṣas, Sarasvatīs, Vedas and poets, would still not reach the end of them.
lanka.101.do101क: Of its many glories dull-witted Tulasīdāsa has told a few,
just as a fly rises into the sky only as far as its own strength allows.
lanka.101.do101ख: His heads and arms were cut off many times, yet the warrior lord of Laṅkā did not die.
The Lord is at play, but gods, siddhas and sages are distressed to see the ordeal.
lanka.102.cau1: As they are cut, the heads multiply, as greed grows with every gain.
The enemy would not die and the toil had grown great; then Śrī Rāma looked towards Vibhīṣaṇa.
lanka.102.cau2: Umā, the Lord at whose will Death itself dies is testing his servant's love.
Vibhīṣaṇa said: Listen, all-knowing one, lord of all that moves and does not move, protector of those who bow to you, giver of joy to gods and sages.
lanka.102.cau3: In the hollow of his navel lies nectar; it is by its power, my Lord, that Rāvaṇa lives.
On hearing Vibhīṣaṇa's words, the compassionate Lord gladly took up fearsome arrows in his hand.
lanka.102.cau4: Then ill omens of many kinds began: donkeys, jackals and many dogs howled;
birds cried out, foretelling distress for the world, and comets appeared here and there in the sky.
lanka.102.cau5: A fierce burning glow spread through all ten quarters, and the sun was eclipsed though it was not the day for it.
Mandodarī's heart trembled violently, and the images shed water from their eyes.
lanka.102.cha1: Images wept, thunderbolts fell from the sky, a fierce wind blew and the earth quaked.
Clouds rained blood, hair and dust; who could tell how many ill omens there were?
Seeing countless portents, the gods in the sky grew distraught and cried: Victory! Victory!
Knowing the gods to be afraid, the compassionate Lord fitted arrows to his bow.
lanka.102.do102: Drawing the bow back to his ear, he loosed thirty-one arrows.
Śrī Rāma's arrows sped on like great serpents of death.
lanka.103.cau1: One arrow dried up the pool at his navel; the others struck his arms and heads in fury.
The arrows went off carrying the heads and arms, and the trunk, without heads or arms, danced upon the ground.
lanka.103.cau2: The trunk rushed about so fiercely that the earth sank beneath it; then the Lord struck it with an arrow and cut it in two.
Dying, he roared with a great and terrible cry: Where is Rāma? Let me challenge him and kill him in battle.
lanka.103.cau3: As Rāvaṇa fell, the earth shook, and the oceans, rivers, elephants of the quarters and mountains were thrown into turmoil.
He fell to the ground with his two halves stretched out, crushing hosts of bears and monkeys beneath them.
lanka.103.cau4: The arrows laid the arms and heads before Mandodarī and went back to where the Lord of the world was.
They all went and entered the quiver; seeing this, the gods beat their kettledrums.
lanka.103.cau5: His radiance passed into the Lord's face; seeing it, Śiva and four-faced Brahmā rejoiced.
The whole universe rang with the cry of victory: Glory to the hero of the Raghus, mighty of arm!
lanka.103.cau6: Hosts of gods and sages shower flowers: Glory to the compassionate one, glory, glory to Mukunda!
lanka.103.cha1: Glory to you, Lord, source of grace, Mukunda, remover of the pairs of opposites, giver of joy to those who come for refuge;
destroyer of the hosts of the wicked, supreme cause, ever compassionate, all-pervading one.
The gods, full of joy, shower flowers, and kettledrums resound loudly.
On the field of battle Śrī Rāma's limbs took on the beauty of many Kāmadevas.
lanka.103.cha2: On his head the crown of matted locks, with flowers here and there among them, looks most lovely,
as if stars were shining with sheets of lightning on a blue mountain.
As he twirls arrows and bow with his mighty arms, the drops of blood on his body look very fine,
as if red munia birds were perched on a tamāla tree in great contentment.
lanka.103.do103: Showering his gracious glance upon them, the Lord freed the hosts of gods from fear.
All the bears and monkeys rejoiced: Glory to Mukunda, abode of joy!
lanka.104.cau1: At the sight of her husband's heads Mandodarī fainted in anguish and fell to the ground.
Crowds of young women rose and ran, weeping; they lifted her up and came to Rāvaṇa.
lanka.104.cau2: Seeing their husband's state, they cried aloud; their hair came loose and they took no care of their bodies.
They beat their breasts in many ways and, weeping, recounted his might.
lanka.104.cau3: They said: My lord, by your might the earth was ever trembling, and fire, moon and sun lost their brightness.
That body whose weight Śeṣa and the cosmic tortoise could not bear lies on the ground, covered in dust.
lanka.104.cau4: Varuṇa, Kubera, Indra and the Wind: not one of them could stand firm before you in battle.
By the strength of your arms, my lord, you conquered Time and Yama; today you lie like one who has no protector.
lanka.104.cau5: Your lordship is known throughout the world; the strength of your sons and kin is beyond telling.
Turned away from Śrī Rāma, you have come to such a state that not one of your line is left to mourn you.
lanka.104.cau6: My lord, all of Brahmā's creation was under your sway, and the guardians of the quarters, afraid, bowed down to you every day.
Now jackals eat your heads and arms; there is nothing improper in this for one who turns from Śrī Rāma.
lanka.104.cau7: Under the sway of Death, my husband, you would not heed what you were told, and took the Lord of all things moving and unmoving for a man.
lanka.104.cha1: You took for a man Śrī Hari himself, the fire that burns the forest of demons.
Beloved, you did not worship the compassionate one, to whom Śiva, Brahmā and the gods bow.
From birth this body of yours delighted in harming others and was full of a flood of sins.
Even to you Śrī Rāma has given his own abode; I bow to Rāma, the Brahman free from every ill.
lanka.104.do104: Ah, my lord, there is no other ocean of mercy like Śrī Rāma.
The Lord has given you the state that hosts of yogīs find hard to attain.
lanka.105.cau1: Hearing Mandodarī's words, gods, sages and siddhas all were glad.
Brahmā, Maheśa, Nārada, Sanaka and his brothers, and all the great sages who speak of the highest truth
lanka.105.cau2: gazed their fill on Śrī Rāma and, lost in love, were all filled with joy.
Vibhīṣaṇa saw all the women weeping, and went to them with a heavy heart.
lanka.105.cau3: Seeing his brother's state, he grieved; then the Lord gave a command to his younger brother.
Lakṣmaṇa consoled him in many ways, and then Vibhīṣaṇa came back to the Lord.
lanka.105.cau4: The Lord turned a gracious glance on him and said: Leave off all grief and carry out the last rites.
Obeying the Lord's command, and bearing in mind the place and the time, he performed the rites as prescribed.
lanka.105.do105: Mandodarī and all the others offered him libations of sesame and water,
and went to the palace, recounting in their minds the many virtues of Śrī Rāma.
lanka.106.cau1: Vibhīṣaṇa came and bowed his head again; then the ocean of mercy called his younger brother.
He said: You, Sugrīva, king of the monkeys, Aṅgada, Nala, Nīla, Jāmbavān and Hanumān, wise in counsel,
lanka.106.cau2: go all together with Vibhīṣaṇa and perform his installation, said Śrī Rāma.
Bound by my father's word, I do not enter a city; so I send the monkeys and my brother, who are as my own self.
lanka.106.cau3: The monkeys left at once on hearing the Lord's words, and there they set about arranging the coronation.
They respectfully placed Vibhīṣaṇa on the throne, and once the tilaka was done they began to sing his praise.
lanka.106.cau4: All of them bowed their heads with joined palms, and came with Vibhīṣaṇa to the Lord.
Then Śrī Rāma called the monkeys to him and, speaking kind words, made them all happy.
lanka.106.cha1: He made them happy with words like nectar: It is by your strength that the enemy has been slain.
Vibhīṣaṇa has gained the kingdom, and your fame will stay ever new in the three worlds.
Those who sing with deep love of your auspicious glory together with mine
will cross the boundless ocean of worldly existence without effort.
lanka.106.do106: The hosts of monkeys hear the Lord's words and cannot have enough of them.
Again and again they all bow their heads and clasp his lotus feet.
lanka.107.cau1: Then the Lord called Hanumān to him. The Lord said: Go to Laṅkā.
Tell Jānakī the news, and come back with word of her welfare.
lanka.107.cau2: Then Hanumān came into the city; hearing of it, the demons and demonesses came running.
They honoured him in many ways, and then showed him Janaka's daughter.
lanka.107.cau3: Hanumān bowed to her from a distance, and Jānakī knew him for Śrī Rāma's messenger.
Sītā said: Tell me, dear one, is all well with the Lord, abode of grace, and his younger brother and the monkey army?
lanka.107.cau4: Hanumān said: Mother, the Lord of Kosala is well in every way; he has conquered Rāvaṇa in battle.
Vibhīṣaṇa has gained a kingdom that will not be shaken. Hearing Hanumān's words, Sītā's heart filled with joy.
lanka.107.cha1: Her mind overjoyed, her body thrilling, her eyes full of tears, Sītā, who is Ramā herself, said again and again:
What can I give you, Hanumān? In the three worlds there is nothing at all to equal these words.
Hanumān said: Listen, Mother: today, beyond doubt, I have gained the kingdom of the whole world,
for I see Śrī Rāma, victorious in battle over the enemy host, safe and well, with his brother.
lanka.107.do107: Sītā said: Listen, my son Hanumān: may every virtue make its home in your heart,
and may the king of Kosala, together with Lakṣmaṇa, who is Ananta, always look on you with favour.
lanka.108.cau1: Now, dear son, make such an effort that my eyes may see the Lord in his dark and tender form.
Then Hanumān went to Śrī Rāma and told him that Sītā was well.
lanka.108.cau2: Hearing the message, the ornament of the solar race sent for Prince Aṅgada and Vibhīṣaṇa and said:
Go with the son of the Wind, and bring Sītā here with due honour.
lanka.108.cau3: They all went straight to Sītā; every one of the demonesses there was serving her meekly.
Vibhīṣaṇa quickly instructed them, and they bathed her with every kind of care.
lanka.108.cau4: They put many kinds of ornaments on her, then made ready a fine palanquin and brought it.
Remembering the loving Śrī Rāma, the abode of bliss, Sītā joyfully mounted it.
lanka.108.cau5: Guards with canes in hand walked on every side, and all went along with hearts full of joy.
The bears and monkeys all came to see her, and the guards rushed angrily to hold them off.
lanka.108.cau6: Śrī Rāma said: Friend, do as I say: bring Sītā on foot,
so that the monkeys may look on her as on a mother. So the Lord Śrī Rāma said, smiling.
lanka.108.cau7: The bears and monkeys rejoiced at the Lord's words, and the gods showered many flowers from the sky.
Sītā had earlier been placed in the fire; now the Witness within all wished to bring her forth.
lanka.108.do108: For this reason the treasury of compassion spoke a few harsh words.
Hearing them, all the demonesses began to grieve.
lanka.109.cau1: Sītā, pure in mind, deed and word, took the Lord's words upon her head and said:
Lakṣmaṇa, assist me in this rite of dharma, and kindle a fire at once.
lanka.109.cau2: Lakṣmaṇa heard Sītā's words, steeped in the pain of separation, in discernment, in dharma and in right counsel.
His eyes filled with tears and he stood with palms joined; he too could say nothing to the Lord.
lanka.109.cau3: Seeing Śrī Rāma's look, Lakṣmaṇa ran, kindled the fire and brought plenty of wood.
Seeing the fierce fire, Sītā felt joy in her heart, and no fear at all.
lanka.109.cau4: Sītā said: If in mind, word and deed there is in my heart no refuge other than Śrī Rāma,
then may Fire, who knows the state of every heart, be as sandalwood to me.
lanka.109.cha1: Remembering the Lord, Sītā, the princess of Mithilā, entered the fire as if it were sandalwood.
She hailed the Lord of Kosala, whose feet, worshipped by Śiva, she loves with a love wholly pure.
Her reflected image and the stain of worldly reproach burned away in the blazing fire.
No one perceived the Lord's play; gods, siddhas and sages stood in the sky, watching.
lanka.109.cha2: Then Fire took a bodily form and held the hand of the true Śrī (Sītā), known to the Vedas and the world,
and, as the Ocean of Milk once gave Indirā to Viṣṇu, brought her and gave her to Śrī Rāma.
She shone at Śrī Rāma's left side, her beauty exceedingly lovely,
as though a bud of golden lotus stood beside a fresh blue lotus.
lanka.109.do109क: The gods joyfully shower flowers, and kettledrums sound in the sky.
Kinnaras sing, and celestial women dance, riding in their aerial cars.
lanka.109.do109ख: The beauty of the Lord with Sītā is measureless and boundless.
Seeing it, the bears and monkeys rejoiced and cried: Glory to the Lord of the Raghus, essence of all joy!
lanka.110.cau1: Then, given leave by Śrī Rāma, Mātali bowed his head at his feet and departed.
Then came the gods, ever intent on their own ends, speaking as if they sought only the highest good.
lanka.110.cau2: Friend of the lowly, compassionate king of the Raghus, O God, you have shown mercy to the gods.
Bent on enmity against the whole world, this lustful villain, who walked the crooked path, has fallen by his own sin.
lanka.110.cau3: You are the imperishable Brahman, the same in form, ever unvarying and by nature detached;
without parts, beyond the guṇas, unborn, sinless, untouched by ill, unconquerable, of unfailing power and full of compassion.
lanka.110.cau4: You took the forms of the Fish, the Tortoise, the Boar, the Man-Lion, the Dwarf and Paraśurāma.
Whenever the gods have suffered, my Lord, you yourself have taken many bodies and ended it.
lanka.110.cau5: This wicked one was impure, ever hostile to the gods, sunk in desire, greed and pride, and full of wrath;
that this chief of the vile should attain your state fills our minds with wonder.
lanka.110.cau6: We gods, though highly qualified, were bent on self-interest and forgot devotion to the Lord.
We have always been caught in the current of worldly existence. Now, Lord, we have come for refuge: protect us.
lanka.110.do110: Their prayer made, all the gods and siddhas stood where they were with palms joined.
Then Brahmā, his body thrilling with deep love, began to praise him:
lanka.111.cha1: Glory to you, Rāma, ever the home of bliss, O Hari, O Lord of the Raghus who bears bow and arrows.
O Lord, you are a lion to the elephant of worldly existence, splitting it apart; ocean of virtues, all-wise, Master, all-pervading one.
lanka.111.cau2: Your form has the beauty of many Kāmadevas and is beyond compare; siddhas, great sages and poets sing your virtues.
Your glory purifies; as Garuḍa in anger seizes a great serpent, so you seized Rāvaṇa.
lanka.111.cau3: Lord, you delight your devotees and break their grief and fear; you are ever free of anger, pure awareness.
Your incarnation is noble and of boundless virtues; you destroy the earth's burden and are knowledge in its fullness.
lanka.111.cau4: Unborn, all-pervading, one, ever without beginning: compassionate Rāma, I bow to you with joy.
Ornament of Raghu's line, slayer of Dūṣaṇa, you made a king of the lowly Vibhīṣaṇa.
lanka.111.cau5: Treasury of virtue and knowledge, free of pride, unborn, all-pervading and stainless: Rāma, I bow to you always.
The might and strength of your arms are fierce; you are most skilled in rooting out the hosts of the wicked.
lanka.111.cau6: Kind without cause to the lowly and seeking their good, abode of beauty, I bow to you with Sītā, who is Ramā herself.
You carry souls across worldly existence, you are beyond cause and effect, and you take away the dreadful faults born in the mind.
lanka.111.cau7: You bear lovely arrows, bow and quiver; your eyes are like red lotuses; you are the best of kings.
Temple of joy, beautiful, Lord of Śrī, you quell pride, lust and false attachment.
lanka.111.cau8: You are faultless, undivided, beyond the reach of the senses; you are ever all forms, and yet you have not become all things.
So the Vedas say; it is no idle tale: just as the sun and its light are distinct and yet not distinct.
lanka.111.cau9: All-pervading Lord, these monkeys have all fulfilled their lives, gazing reverently on your face.
Shame on our life and our divine bodies, O Hari, for without devotion to you we lie lost in worldly existence.
lanka.111.cau10: Compassionate to the lowly, show mercy now and take away my mind that makes divisions,
by which I act perversely and, taking that sorrow for joy, go about content.
lanka.111.cau11: You break the wicked and adorn the lovely earth; your lotus feet are served by Śambhu and Umā.
Lord of kings, give me this boon: that I may always have a love for your lotus feet that brings every good.
lanka.111.do111: Brahmā, the four-faced, made his prayer, his body thrilling with love.
Gazing on the ocean of beauty, his eyes could not have their fill.
lanka.112.cau1: At that moment Daśaratha came there; seeing his son, his eyes brimmed with tears.
The Lord and his younger brother bowed to him, and then the father gave his blessing.
lanka.112.cau2: The Lord said: Father, it is all the power of your merit that I have conquered the invincible king of the demons.
Hearing his son's words, his love grew greatly; his eyes filled and the hair on his body stood on end.
lanka.112.cau3: Śrī Rāma, mindful of his father's love of old, looked at him and gave him firm knowledge.
Umā, that is why Daśaratha did not attain liberation: he had set his heart on devotion that keeps the Lord and the devotee distinct.
lanka.112.cau4: Those who worship the Lord with form do not take liberation; to them Śrī Rāma gives devotion to himself.
Bowing to the Lord again and again, Daśaratha went gladly to the abode of the gods.
lanka.112.do112: The Lord of Kosala stood safe and well with his younger brother and Jānakī.
Seeing their beauty, Indra, lord of the gods, rejoiced at heart and began to praise him:
lanka.113.cha1: Glory to you, Rāma, abode of beauty, giver of rest to those who bow before you.
You bear a fine quiver, arrows and bow; your arms are mighty and glorious.
lanka.113.cha2: Glory to you, foe of Dūṣaṇa and Khara, crusher of the demon hosts.
My Lord, you have slain this wicked one, and all the gods now have a protector.
lanka.113.cha3: Glory to you who lift the earth's burden; your greatness is noble and boundless.
Glory to you, merciful foe of Rāvaṇa, who left the demons broken.
lanka.113.cha4: The lord of Laṅkā, swollen with pride in his strength, had brought gods and gandharvas under his sway.
Sages, siddhas, men, birds and nāgas: he stubbornly dogged the steps of them all.
lanka.113.cha5: Given to malice towards others and utterly wicked, that great sinner has reaped his fruit.
Now listen, you who are kind to the lowly, whose eyes are large as lotuses:
lanka.113.cha6: I was full of pride, thinking there was none my equal.
Now that I have seen the Lord's lotus feet, the pride that brought heaps of sorrow is gone.
lanka.113.cha7: Some meditate on Brahman without attributes, whom the Vedas hymn as unmanifest.
But the one I love is the king of Kosala, Śrī Rāma in his form with attributes.
lanka.113.cha8: With Sītā and your younger brother, make your home in my heart.
Know me as your own servant, abode of Ramā, and give me devotion.
lanka.113.cha9: Give me devotion, abode of Ramā, remover of fear, giver of joy to those who seek refuge.
Home of joy, Rāma, Lord of the Raghus, lovely as many Kāmadevas, I bow to you.
Delight of the hosts of gods, destroyer of the pairs of opposites, wearing a human body, of matchless strength,
Rāma, worshipped by Brahmā, Śaṅkara and the rest, tender with compassion, I bow to you.
lanka.113.do113: Now look on me with grace, merciful Lord, and give me your command:
what shall I do? Hearing these pleasing words, the Lord, compassionate to the lowly, spoke:
lanka.114.cau1: Listen, Indra: the monkeys and bears of ours whom the demons killed are lying on the ground.
For my sake they gave up their lives; wise lord of the gods, bring them all back to life.
lanka.114.cau2: Listen, Garuḍa: these words of the Lord are very deep, and only sages rich in knowledge understand them.
The Lord could slay the three worlds and bring them to life again; here he simply gave the honour to Indra.
lanka.114.cau3: Showering nectar, Indra brought the monkeys and bears back to life, and they all rose up joyfully and came to the Lord.
The rain of nectar fell on both armies, yet only the bears and monkeys revived, not the demons.
lanka.114.cau4: The minds of those demons had taken on the form of Śrī Rāma; they were set free, the bonds of worldly existence loosed.
The monkeys and bears were all born of portions of the gods, and all of them revived by the will of Śrī Rāma.
lanka.114.cau5: Who is such a friend to the lowly as Śrī Rāma, who set free the demons, every one of them?
Rāvaṇa, wicked, a home of impurity and given to lust, attained a state that the greatest sages do not attain.
lanka.114.do114क: Having showered flowers, the gods all mounted their beautiful aerial cars and departed.
Seeing that the moment was right, the wise Śiva came to the Lord.
lanka.114.do114ख: With supreme love, joining both his hands, his lotus eyes filled with tears,
his body thrilling and his voice choked, Śiva, the foe of Tripura, prays:
lanka.115.cha1: Protect me, O Lord of Raghu's line, who hold the excellent bow and arrows in your beautiful hands.
You are the wind that scatters the vast, dense veil of the clouds of delusion, the fire to the forest of doubt, the delight of the gods.
lanka.115.cau2: Without attributes and with attributes, abode of virtues and beautiful, you are the sun of mighty splendour to the darkness of error.
Lion to the elephants of desire, anger and pride, dwell for ever in the forest of your devotee's mind.
lanka.115.cau3: To the lotus beds of the throngs of sensual cravings you are a hard frost; you are generous, and beyond the reach of the mind.
Mount Mandara to the ocean of worldly existence, drive away my great fear and carry me across the round of births, so hard to cross.
lanka.115.cau4: Dark of body, lotus-eyed, friend of the lowly, deliverer of those who bow to you from their distress,
O King Rāma, dwell for ever within my heart, with your younger brother and Sītā.
lanka.115.cau5: Joy of the sages, ornament of the circle of the earth, Tulasīdāsa's Lord who shatters fear.
lanka.115.do115: My Lord, when your coronation takes place in the city of Kosala,
I will come, O ocean of mercy, to see your noble deeds.
lanka.116.cau1: When Śiva had made his prayer and departed, Vibhīṣaṇa came close to the Lord.
Bowing his head at his feet, he said in gentle words: My Lord, wielder of the Śārṅga bow, hear my plea.
lanka.116.cau2: My Lord, you have slain Rāvaṇa with his family and his army, and spread your holy fame through the three worlds.
On me, wretched and unclean, poor in understanding and low in birth, you have shown grace in many ways.
lanka.116.cau3: Now, my Lord, sanctify your servant's house; bathe there, and let the weariness of battle fall away.
Look over the treasury, the palaces and the wealth, O compassionate one, and give gladly to the monkeys.
lanka.116.cau4: My Lord, accept me wholly as yours; then, when you go to Ayodhyā, take me along.
As he heard these gentle words, both the large eyes of the Lord, kind to the lowly, filled with tears.
lanka.116.do116क: Śrī Rāma said: Listen, brother, this is the truth: your treasury and your house are all mine.
But when I remember Bharata's state, each moment passes for me like an aeon.
lanka.116.do116ख: In the garb of an ascetic, his body worn thin, he repeats my name without ceasing.
My friend, I beg you, find a way for me to see him soon.
lanka.116.do116ग: If I go when the appointed time has passed, I shall not find my brother alive.
As he remembered his younger brother's love, the Lord's body thrilled again and again.
lanka.116.do116घ: The Lord went on: Rule for a whole aeon, and keep me in mind within your heart.
Then you will reach my abode, where all the saints go.
lanka.117.cau1: Hearing Śrī Rāma's words, Vibhīṣaṇa joyfully clasped the feet of the abode of grace.
All the monkeys and bears rejoiced, and holding the Lord's feet they told of his spotless virtues.
lanka.117.cau2: Then Vibhīṣaṇa went to his palace and had the aerial car loaded with heaps of gems and with clothes.
He brought the Puṣpaka and placed it in front of the Lord; then the ocean of mercy smiled and said:
lanka.117.cau3: Listen, my friend Vibhīṣaṇa: mount the aerial car, go up into the sky and rain down clothes and ornaments.
Vibhīṣaṇa went up into the sky that very moment and rained down every gem and garment.
lanka.117.cau4: Each takes whatever pleases his fancy; the monkeys put the gems in their mouths and spit them out again.
Śrī Rāma laughed, with Sītā and his younger brother, he who delights in play, the abode of grace.
lanka.117.do117क: He whom sages do not reach even in meditation, of whom the Vedas say neti neti, not this, not this,
that same ocean of mercy is sporting in many ways with the monkeys.
lanka.117.do117ख: Umā, for yoga, japa, charity, austerity, many kinds of sacrifice, vows and rules of observance
Śrī Rāma does not show such grace as he does for love, pure and unmixed.
lanka.118.cau1: The bears and monkeys received clothes and ornaments, and decked out in them came to Śrī Rāma.
Seeing all the monkeys in such variety, the Lord of Kosala laughs again and again.
lanka.118.cau2: Looking at them all, Śrī Rāma showed them kindness and spoke gentle words:
By your strength I slew Rāvaṇa, and then crowned Vibhīṣaṇa.
lanka.118.cau3: Now go, all of you, each to your own home; remember me, and fear no one.
Hearing these words, the monkeys were overcome with love, and all of them said with joined palms and respect:
lanka.118.cau4: My Lord, whatever you say becomes you; but hearing such words we are bewildered.
You counted us monkeys poor and lowly and gave us a master in yourself; you, O Lord of the Raghus, rule the three worlds.
lanka.118.cau5: Hearing the Lord's words, we are dying of shame: do mosquitoes ever do Garuḍa a service?
Seeing Śrī Rāma's countenance, the bears and monkeys were lost in love and had no wish to go home.
lanka.118.do118क: At the Lord's prompting, all the monkeys and bears, keeping Śrī Rāma's form in their hearts,
set out with joy and sorrow mingled, after making their humble pleas in many ways.
lanka.118.do118ख: Sugrīva, king of the monkeys, Nīla, Jāmbavān, king of the bears, Aṅgada, Nala and Hanumān,
together with Vibhīṣaṇa and the other mighty monkey troop leaders,
lanka.118.do118ग: could say nothing, overcome by love, their eyes filling with tears again and again.
Facing Śrī Rāma, they gazed at him, holding back even the blink of their eyes.
lanka.119.cau1: Seeing their exceeding love, Śrī Rāma took them all up into the aerial car.
Bowing his head in his heart at the feet of the brāhmaṇas, he set the car moving northward.
lanka.119.cau2: As the car moves off there is a great clamour, everyone crying: Glory to the hero of the Raghus.
There is a throne, very high and lovely; on it the Lord took his seat with Sītā.
lanka.119.cau3: Śrī Rāma with his lady shines as though cloud and lightning rested on a summit of Mount Meru.
The beautiful car sped on in great haste; the gods rejoiced and rained down flowers.
lanka.119.cau4: A most pleasant breeze blew, cool, gentle and fragrant; the waters of ocean, lake and river were pure.
Fair omens appear all around; hearts are glad, and the sky and the quarters are clear.
lanka.119.cau5: Śrī Rāma said: Look at the battlefield, Sītā. Here Lakṣmaṇa slew Meghanāda, conqueror of Indra.
Struck down by Hanumān and Aṅgada, mighty demons lie fallen on the field.
lanka.119.cau6: Kumbhakarṇa and Rāvaṇa, the two brothers who tormented gods and sages, were slain here.
lanka.119.do119क: Here I built the bridge and installed Śiva, the home of bliss.
Then the compassionate Lord, with Sītā, bowed to Śiva.
lanka.119.do119ख: Every place in the forest where the ocean of mercy had stayed and rested
he showed to Sītā, and told her the names of them all.
lanka.120.cau1: Swiftly the car came to where the lovely Daṇḍaka forest lay.
Śrī Rāma went to the dwellings of all the many great sages, Agastya and the rest.
lanka.120.cau2: Having received the blessings of all the seers, the Lord of the world came to Citrakūṭa.
There he gladdened the sages, and the car flew swiftly on from there.
lanka.120.cau3: Next Śrī Rāma showed Sītā the lovely Yamunā, which takes away the taint of the Kali age.
Then they saw the holy Gaṅgā, and Śrī Rāma said: Sītā, bow to her.
lanka.120.cau4: Now see Prayāga, king of holy places, at the sight of which the sins of ten million births take flight.
Then see the most purifying Triveṇī, which takes away grief and is a ladder to the world of Śrī Hari.
lanka.120.cau5: And now see the city of Ayodhyā, most purifying, which destroys the threefold affliction and the disease of worldly existence.
lanka.120.do120क: With Sītā, the compassionate Lord bowed to Ayodhyā.
His eyes filled with tears and his body thrilled; again and again Śrī Rāma was overjoyed.
lanka.120.do120ख: Then the Lord came to the Triveṇī and bathed there joyfully,
and together with the monkeys he gave gifts of many kinds to the brāhmaṇas.
lanka.121.cau1: The Lord explained to Hanumān: Take the form of a young brahmacārī and go to Ayodhyā.
Give Bharata the news that we are well, and come back with news from there.
lanka.121.cau2: Hanumān, son of the Wind, set off at once. Then the Lord went to Bharadvāja.
The sage worshipped him with many rites, sang his praises and then gave his blessing.
lanka.121.cau3: Bowing at the sage's feet with both palms joined, the Lord mounted the aerial car and went on again.
Here the Niṣāda heard that the Lord had come, and called his people, crying: A boat! Where is a boat?
lanka.121.cau4: Then the aerial car came over the Gaṅgā and, at the Lord's command, came down on the bank.
Then Sītā worshipped the Gaṅgā, and after that fell at her feet in many ways.
lanka.121.cau5: Gaṅgā, glad at heart, gave her blessing: Fair lady, may your married happiness never be broken.
As soon as he heard, Guha ran, overcome with love, and came near, brimming with the highest joy.
lanka.121.cau6: Seeing the Lord with Vaidehī, he fell to the ground, aware of his body no longer.
Seeing his great love, Śrī Rāma joyfully raised him up and pressed him to his heart.
lanka.121.cha1: The Lord of Ramā, treasury of mercy, king among the wise, pressed him to his heart,
seated him very close and asked how he was. Then he made his entreaty:
Now that I have seen your lotus feet, which Brahmā and Śaṅkara serve, all is well with me.
O Rāma, abode of joy, whose every wish is fulfilled, I bow to you; Rāma, I bow to you.
lanka.121.cha2: Śrī Hari pressed the Niṣāda, lowly in every way, to his heart as he would Bharata.
Dull-witted Tulasīdāsa, in the grip of delusion, has forgotten such a Lord.
This holy story of Śrī Rāma, Rāvaṇa's foe, ever grants love for Śrī Rāma's feet.
It takes away desire and the other passions and gives realised knowledge; gods, siddhas and sages sing it with joy.
lanka.121.do121क: To those of understanding who hear the deeds of Śrī Rāma's victory in battle,
the Lord gives victory, discernment and prosperity, day after day.
lanka.121.do121ख: This age of Kali is a home of impurity: reflect in your mind and see.
Apart from the name of Śrī Rāma, there is no other support.
uttar.0.shloka1: I bow ceaselessly to him who is blue as a peacock's throat, the best of the gods, adorned with the print of the Brahmin's (Bhṛgu's) lotus foot,
rich in beauty, clad in yellow, lotus-eyed, at all times full of gladness;
who holds arrow and bow in his hand, with hosts of monkeys about him, served by his brother;
the adorable lord of Jānakī, the best of the Raghus, Rāma seated on the Puṣpaka.
uttar.0.shloka2: The two lotus feet of the king of Kosala are lovely and tender, worshipped by Brahmā and the great Śiva;
caressed by Jānakī's lotus hands, they are the companions of the bee that is the mind of one who meditates on them.
uttar.0.shloka3: Fair and handsome as jasmine, the moon and the conch, the husband of Ambikā, the giver of the success one longs for,
compassionate, with lovely lotus eyes: I bow to Śaṅkara, who sets one free from Kāma, the god of desire.
uttar.0.dou1: Only one day of the appointed term was left, and the people of the city were in deep distress.
Everywhere women and men, worn thin by separation from Śrī Rāma, were sunk in anxious thought.
uttar.0.dou2: Fair omens of every kind appeared, and everyone's heart was glad.
As if announcing the Lord's coming, the city grew delightful on every side.
uttar.0.dou3: Kausalyā and all the other mothers felt such joy in their hearts
as if someone were just about to tell them: The Lord has come, with Sītā and his younger brother.
uttar.0.dou4: Again and again Bharata's right eye and his right arm quivered.
Taking it for a good omen, he was overjoyed at heart, and he began to ponder.
uttar.1.cau1: Of the term that was his one support only a day remained; as he grasped this, his mind filled with boundless grief.
What can be the reason that my Lord has not come? Or has he forgotten me, knowing me to be crooked?
uttar.1.cau2: Ah, blessed and fortunate is Lakṣmaṇa, who loves the lotus feet of Śrī Rāma.
The Lord saw that I am deceitful and crooked, and so my master did not take me along.
uttar.1.cau3: Were the Lord to judge me by what I have done, a thousand million kalpas would not see me saved.
But the Lord never holds his servant's faults against him; he is the friend of the lowly, and his nature is very gentle.
uttar.1.cau4: In my heart there is that one firm trust: I shall meet Śrī Rāma; the omens too are good.
If my life remains once the term is past, who in the world will be as base as I?
uttar.1.do1क: In the ocean of Śrī Rāma's absence Bharata's mind was going under,
and just then the son of the Wind arrived, dressed as a Brahmin, as though a ship had come.
uttar.1.do1ख: He saw Bharata seated on a mat of kuśa grass, his matted locks for a crown, his body worn thin,
repeating Rāma, Rāma, Raghupati, tears flowing from his lotus eyes.
uttar.2.cau1: At the sight Hanumān rejoiced greatly; his body thrilled and his eyes rained tears.
Delighted in his heart in many ways, he spoke words that were like nectar to the ears:
uttar.2.cau2: He for whom you grieve day and night in separation, whose virtues you recite without pause, row upon row,
the jewel of Raghu's line, the giver of joy to the good, the protector of gods and sages, has come safe and well.
uttar.2.cau3: He has conquered the enemy in battle, the gods sing his fair fame, and the Lord is on his way with Sītā and his younger brother.
Hearing this, Bharata forgot every sorrow, as one parched with thirst does on finding nectar.
uttar.2.cau4: Bharata said: Who are you, dear friend, and where have you come from? You have told me the dearest of news.
Hanumān said: Hear my name, O treasury of compassion: I am Hanumān, a monkey, son of the Wind.
uttar.2.cau5: I am a servant of Śrī Rāma, the friend of the lowly. At these words Bharata stood up and, with great respect, held him to his heart.
As they met, his heart could not hold his love; tears streamed from his eyes and his body thrilled.
uttar.2.cau6: Bharata said: Hanumān, at the sight of you all my sorrows are over; today I have met my beloved Śrī Rāma.
Again and again he asked how all were, and said: Listen, brother, what can I give you?
uttar.2.cau7: I have thought it over and found nothing in the world to equal this message.
Dear friend, I can never be free of my debt to you. Now tell me the story of the Lord.
uttar.2.cau8: Then Hanumān, his head bowed at Bharata's feet, told him all the tale of Śrī Rāma's virtues.
Bharata said: Tell me, Hanumān, does my compassionate master ever remember me as his servant?
uttar.2.cha1: Has the jewel of the Raghu line ever remembered me as his own servant?
Hearing Bharata's most humble words, Hanumān, his body thrilling, fell at his feet.
One whose many virtues Śrī Rāma, lord of all that moves and all that is still, tells of with his own lips,
how could he not be humble, supremely pure, an ocean of good qualities?
uttar.2.do2क: Hanumān said: My lord, you are as dear to Śrī Rāma as his own life; what I say is true, dear one.
Hearing this, Bharata embraced him again and again, his heart unable to contain its joy.
uttar.2.so2ख: Hanumān bowed his head at Bharata's feet and hurried straight back to Śrī Rāma.
Reaching him, he gave the news that all were well; then the Lord, glad at heart, mounted the aerial car and set off.
uttar.3.cau1: Bharata came joyfully back to the city of Kosala and gave his guru all the news.
Then he made it known in the palace that Śrī Rāma was coming to the city safe and well.
uttar.3.cau2: Hearing it, all the mothers rose and ran; Bharata told them the Lord was well and reassured them.
When the townspeople had the news, all of them, men and women, ran out in joy.
uttar.3.cau3: Curds, dūrvā grass, gorocana, fruit, flowers and fresh tulasī leaves, the root of all blessing:
heaping these on golden platters, women moving with an elephant's graceful gait went out singing.
uttar.3.cau4: Everyone runs out just as they are, not stopping to bring children or the old along.
They ask one another: Brother, have you seen Śrī Rāma, the compassionate?
uttar.3.cau5: Ayodhyā, knowing the Lord was on his way, became a treasure-house of every kind of beauty.
A pleasant breeze blew, cool, gentle and fragrant, and the Sarayū's water grew perfectly clear.
uttar.3.do3क: Joyful, with the guru, the family, his younger brother and a throng of Brahmins,
Bharata, his heart full of love, went out to meet Śrī Rāma, the abode of grace.
uttar.3.do3ख: Many women climbed to the upper rooms and gazed at the aerial car in the sky.
Seeing it, they sang auspicious songs in sweet voices, full of joy.
uttar.3.do3ग: Ayodhyā was an ocean that rejoiced at the sight of its full moon, Śrī Rāma;
it swelled with a roar of voices, and the women seemed its waves.
uttar.4.cau1: Here Śrī Rāma, the sun to the lotus of the solar race, was showing the monkeys the lovely city.
He said: Listen, Sugrīva, Aṅgada and Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of Laṅkā. This city is holy and this land is beautiful.
uttar.4.cau2: Though all have praised Vaikuṇṭha, which the Vedas and Purāṇas make known and the world knows of,
even it is not as dear to me as Ayodhyā; only a rare few understand this.
uttar.4.cau3: This lovely city is where I was born; the holy Sarayū flows along its northern side,
and whoever bathes in it comes, with no labour at all, to live close to me.
uttar.4.cau4: The people who live here are very dear to me; this city is a store of happiness and bestows my own abode.
All the monkeys rejoiced to hear the Lord's words: blessed is Ayodhyā, which Śrī Rāma has praised.
uttar.4.do4क: The Lord, the ocean of mercy, saw all the people coming,
and he directed the aerial car; it came down to the ground near the city.
uttar.4.do4ख: When he had alighted, the Lord said to Puṣpaka: Go to Kubera.
At Śrī Rāma's bidding it set off, glad, yet sorely grieved to be parted from him.
uttar.5.cau1: All the people came with Bharata, their bodies worn thin by separation from Śrī Rāma.
The Lord saw Vāmadeva and Vasiṣṭha, chief among sages, and laying his bow and arrows on the ground,
uttar.5.cau2: he ran to his guru and caught hold of his lotus feet; he and his younger brother thrilled from head to foot.
The king of sages embraced him and asked if all was well. The Lord said: We are well by your mercy alone.
uttar.5.cau3: Śrī Rāma, lord of Raghu's line and upholder of dharma, greeted all the Brahmins with a bow of the head.
Next Bharata took hold of those lotus feet of the Lord before which gods, sages, Śiva and Brahmā bow.
uttar.5.cau4: He lay on the ground and would not rise when they tried to lift him; then the ocean of mercy raised him by force and held him to his heart.
The hair on the Lord's dark body stood on end, and his eyes, like fresh lotuses, brimmed with tears.
uttar.5.cha1: Tears flow from his lotus eyes, and the hair on his lovely body stands on end.
With deep love the Lord, master of the three worlds, held his younger brother to his heart.
How the Lord looks as he meets his brother, I cannot find a likeness to tell.
It is as if love and śṛṅgāra, the spirit of beauty, had taken bodies and met, and gained a matchless loveliness.
uttar.5.cha2: The treasury of mercy asks Bharata how he is, but words do not come quickly to him.
Listen, Śivā: that joy lies beyond words and mind; only one who finds it knows it.
Bharata said: All is well now, Lord of Kosala; knowing your servant to be in distress, you have given him the sight of you.
As I was drowning in the ocean of separation, the treasury of compassion took me by the hand.
uttar.5.do5: Then the Lord joyfully embraced Śatrughna, holding him to his heart.
Then Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata, the two brothers, met in the deepest love.
uttar.6.cau1: Then Lakṣmaṇa embraced Bharata's younger brother, ending the unbearable grief that separation had brought.
Bharata bowed his head at Sītā's feet and, with his younger brother, found the highest joy.
uttar.6.cau2: The townspeople rejoiced to see the Lord; all the hardship born of separation vanished.
Seeing everyone restless with love, the compassionate Śrī Rāma, slayer of Khara, worked a wonder.
uttar.6.cau3: At that moment the compassionate Lord appeared in countless forms and met each person as was fitting.
Śrī Rāma looked on them with grace and freed every man and woman from sorrow.
uttar.6.cau4: In an instant the Lord met everyone; Umā, no one knew this secret.
Having thus made all happy, Śrī Rāma, the home of goodness and virtue, went on ahead.
uttar.6.cau5: Kausalyā and all the mothers ran, like newly calved cows that catch sight of their calves.
uttar.6.cha1: It was as if cows had left their young calves at home and gone, against their will, to graze in the forest,
and at the end of the day ran lowing towards the town, milk dripping from their udders.
With deep love the Lord met all the mothers and spoke gentle words to them in many ways.
The harsh hardship born of separation was gone, and they found joy and happiness beyond count.
uttar.6.do6क: Sumitrā embraced her son, knowing his love for Śrī Rāma's feet.
Meeting Śrī Rāma, Kaikeyī felt deeply abashed at heart.
uttar.6.do6ख: Lakṣmaṇa met all the mothers and rejoiced to receive their blessings.
He met Kaikeyī again and again, yet the unrest in his mind would not go.
uttar.7.cau1: Sītā met all her mothers-in-law, and touching their feet she was filled with joy.
Asking after her welfare, they bless her: May your married happiness stay unshaken.
uttar.7.cau2: They all gaze on Śrī Rāma's lotus face and, knowing the hour to be auspicious, hold back the tears in their eyes.
They wave the lamps on golden platters and look again and again at the Lord's form.
uttar.7.cau3: They make offerings over him in many ways, and their hearts fill with supreme bliss and joy.
Again and again Kausalyā looks at Śrī Rāma, the ocean of mercy, steadfast in battle.
uttar.7.cau4: She wonders in her heart again and again: How did he kill the lord of Laṅkā?
My two boys are so tender, and the demons were great warriors of immense strength.
uttar.7.do7: The mother gazes at the Lord with Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā;
her heart is immersed in supreme bliss, and again and again her body thrills.
uttar.8.cau1: Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of Laṅkā, Sugrīva, king of the monkeys, Nala, Nīla, Jāmbavān and the noble Aṅgada,
Hanumān and all the other monkey heroes had taken on charming human forms.
uttar.8.cau2: Bharata's affection, his goodness, his vows and his discipline: all of them tell of these with reverence and deep love.
Seeing the ways of the townsfolk, they all praise their love for the Lord's feet.
uttar.8.cau3: Then Śrī Rāma called all his friends and taught them all: Bow at the sage's feet.
This is Guru Vasiṣṭha, revered by our family; by his grace the demons were slain in battle.
uttar.8.cau4: Listen, sage: these are all my friends; in the ocean of battle they became my rafts.
For my good they put their lives at stake; I hold them dearer even than Bharata.
uttar.8.cau5: Hearing the Lord's words they were all overwhelmed; with every moment fresh joys rose in them.
uttar.8.do8क: Next they bent their heads at Kausalyā's feet.
She blessed them with joy: You are as dear to me as Rāma.
uttar.8.do8ख: Flowers rained down till the sky was thick with them, and Śrī Rāma, the source of joy, went on towards the palace.
Crowds of the city's women and men climbed to the balconies to watch him.
uttar.9.cau1: Everyone adorned golden pitchers in wonderful ways and set them, decked, at their own doors.
For good fortune all put up festoons, banners and flags.
uttar.9.cau2: All the lanes were sprinkled with fragrance, and many auspicious squares were drawn with elephant-pearls.
Auspicious things of every kind were arranged, and in joy many kettledrums sounded through the city.
uttar.9.cau3: Everywhere women make offerings over him and, hearts brimming with joy, give their blessings.
Young women arrange many lamps on golden platters and sing auspicious songs.
uttar.9.cau4: They wave the lamps before the remover of distress, the sun to the lotus-forest of the Raghu line.
The Vedas, Śeṣa and Sarasvatī have described the beauty, wealth and well-being of the city;
uttar.9.cau5: yet even they are left spellbound at the sight of this; then how, Umā, can mortals tell of his virtues?
uttar.9.do9क: The women were night-lotuses in the lake of Ayodhyā, and separation from Śrī Rāma was the sun;
now that it has set, they have blossomed at the sight of the moon that is Śrī Rāma.
uttar.9.do9ख: Good omens of many kinds appear, and drums sound in the sky.
Having given the men and women of the city their lord again, the Lord went on to the palace.
uttar.10.cau1: Knowing that Kaikeyī was ashamed, Pārvatī, the Lord went first to her house.
He comforted her and gave her great happiness, and then Śrī Hari went to his own palace.
uttar.10.cau2: When the ocean of mercy entered the palace, all the men and women of the city were happy.
Guru Vasiṣṭha sent for the Brahmins and said: Today the hour is good, the day is good, everything has come together.
uttar.10.cau3: All you Brahmins, gladly give your command that Śrī Rāma take his seat on the throne.
The sage Vasiṣṭha's pleasing words delighted all the Brahmins as soon as they heard them.
uttar.10.cau4: Many Brahmins said in gentle words: Śrī Rāma's coronation gladdens the whole world.
Now, best of sages, make no delay; place the mark of kingship on the Mahārāja's brow.
uttar.10.do10क: Then the sage spoke to Sumantra, who set off gladly as soon as he heard,
and going at once he had many chariots, horses and elephants made ready.
uttar.10.do10ख: Then, sending runners here and there, he had auspicious things brought,
and coming back he joyfully bowed his head at Vasiṣṭha's feet.
uttar.11.cau1: The city of Ayodhyā was decked most beautifully, and the gods let fall a steady shower of flowers.
Śrī Rāma sent for his servants and told them: First go and bathe my friends.
uttar.11.cau2: At these words people ran here and there and at once bathed Sugrīva and the rest.
Then Śrī Rāma, treasury of compassion, called Bharata and with his own hands untangled his matted hair.
uttar.11.cau3: The Lord, the gracious Śrī Rāma who loves his devotees, bathed all three brothers.
Bharata's good fortune and the Lord's tenderness could not be sung by a thousand million Śeṣas.
uttar.11.cau4: Then Śrī Rāma untangled his own matted locks and, asking the Guru's leave, bathed.
After bathing the Lord put on his ornaments; seeing his limbs, a hundred Kāmadevas felt ashamed.
uttar.11.do11क: With honour the mothers-in-law quickly bathed Sītā,
and dressed every limb with care in heavenly garments and fine ornaments.
uttar.11.do11ख: On Śrī Rāma's left shines Ramā (Sītā), a mine of beauty and virtue.
Seeing it, all the mothers rejoiced, counting their lives fulfilled.
uttar.11.do11ग: Listen, Garuḍa: at that time Brahmā, Śiva, hosts of sages
and all the gods came mounted on their aerial chariots to see the source of joy.
uttar.12.cau1: Seeing the Lord, the sage's heart filled with love, and at once he called for a heavenly throne.
Its radiance, like the sun's, was beyond words; Śrī Rāma bowed to the Brahmins and sat upon it.
uttar.12.cau2: Seeing Śrī Rāma with Sītā, daughter of Janaka, the whole company of sages rejoiced greatly.
Then the Brahmins chanted Vedic mantras, and in the sky gods and sages cried out: Victory, victory!
uttar.12.cau3: First the sage Vasiṣṭha applied the tilaka, then he gave leave to all the Brahmins.
The mothers rejoiced to see their son and waved the lamps before him again and again.
uttar.12.cau4: The Brahmins received gifts of many kinds, and every beggar was made one who need never beg.
Seeing the master of the three worlds on the throne, the gods beat their drums.
uttar.12.cha1: Countless drums sound in the sky; gandharvas and kinnaras sing.
Troupes of apsarās dance, and gods and sages find supreme bliss.
Bharata and the other younger brothers, with Vibhīṣaṇa, Aṅgada, Hanumān and the rest,
stand resplendent, holding the parasol, the whisk, the fan, the bow, the sword, the shield and the spear.
uttar.12.cha2: With Sītā beside him, the jewel of the solar line shines with the beauty of many Kāmadevas.
The yellow garment on his beautiful body, dark as a fresh rain-cloud, enchants the minds of the gods.
Crown, armlets and other wonderful ornaments adorn every limb.
His eyes are lotuses, his chest and arms are mighty; blessed are those who behold him.
uttar.12.do12क: Garuḍa, that splendour, that assembly and that joy cannot be told.
Sarasvatī, Śeṣa and the Vedas describe it, and its savour is known to Maheśa.
uttar.12.do12ख: Each offering his own praise, the gods went back to their own realms.
Then the Vedas, in the guise of bards, came to where Śrī Rāma was.
uttar.12.do12ग: The all-knowing Lord, the treasury of mercy, received them with great honour.
No one grasped the secret at all, and they began to sing his praises.
uttar.13.cha1: Glory to you, who are with form and beyond form, of form beyond compare, crest-jewel of kings.
By the strength of your arms you slew Rāvaṇa and the other fierce, mighty and wicked demons.
Taking birth as a man, you broke the burden of the world and burned away its cruel sorrows.
Glory to you, compassionate Lord, protector of those who bow to you; we bow to you together with your Śakti, Sītā.
uttar.13.cha2: O Hari, gods and demons, nāgas and men, all that moves and does not move, under the sway of your hard māyā (the Lord's power of illusion),
wander for countless days and nights on the road of worldly existence, filled with time, karma and the guṇas.
Those on whom you have looked with compassion, my Lord, are freed from the threefold suffering.
O Rāma, skilled in cutting away the weariness of worldly existence, protect us; we bow to you.
uttar.13.cha3: Those who, drunk with pride of knowledge, did not honour devotion to you, which ends worldly existence,
we see, O Hari, win a state hard even for the gods to reach, and fall from it.
Those who trust you, give up every other hope, and remain your servants
cross the ocean of worldly existence without toil by repeating your name; it is you, our Lord, whom we remember.
uttar.13.cha4: The feet that Śiva and Brahmā worship, whose holy dust, once it touched her, set free the sage's wife,
from whose nails came the Gaṅgā, river of the gods, revered by sages, purifier of the three worlds,
which bear the banner, the thunderbolt, the goad and the lotus, and grew calluses from thorns as they walked the forest:
those two lotus feet, O Mukunda, O Rāma, O lord of Ramā, we ever worship.
uttar.13.cha5: The Vedas and scriptures tell of a beginningless tree whose root is the Unmanifest, with four barks,
six trunks, twenty-five branches, countless leaves and thick flowers,
two kinds of fruit, bitter and sweet, and a single creeper that lives clinging to it,
ever putting out fresh shoots and flowers: to that tree of worldly existence we bow.
uttar.13.cha6: Some meditate on Brahman as unborn, non-dual, known by experience alone, beyond the mind:
let them speak of it and know it so; we, my Lord, ever sing the glory of your form with attributes.
Lord, home of compassion, mine of virtues, O God, this is the boon we ask:
that, casting off the faults of mind, speech and action, we may love your feet.
uttar.13.do13क: While all looked on, the Vedas made this noble prayer;
then they vanished and went to the abode of Brahmā.
uttar.13.do13ख: Listen, Garuḍa: then Śiva came to where Śrī Rāma was,
and made his prayer with a voice choked with feeling, his whole body thrilling.
uttar.14.cha1: Glory to you, Rāma, beloved of Ramā, who brings peace; save your servant, troubled by fear of the fever of worldly existence.
Lord of Avadh, lord of the gods, lord of Ramā, all-pervading one: I have come for refuge and I ask you, Lord, save me.
uttar.14.cau2: Destroyer of the ten-headed, twenty-armed one, you have taken away the earth's great and grievous ills.
The hosts of demons were moths, burned up in the fierce blaze of the fire of your arrows.
uttar.14.cau3: Lovelier than all, the ornament of the earth's circle, you bear the noble arrows, bow and quiver.
To the dense darkness of the great night of pride, delusion and possessiveness, you are the host of the sun's rays.
uttar.14.cau4: Kāma, the hunter, has struck down the deer that are people, piercing their hearts with the arrows of base pleasures.
Slay him, my Lord, O Hari, and save these helpless ones, wretches who have strayed and fallen in the forest of the senses.
uttar.14.cau5: People are struck down by many diseases and partings; these are the fruits of disregarding your feet.
Those men lie in the fathomless ocean of worldly existence who have no love for your lotus feet.
uttar.14.cau6: Ever most wretched, sullied and sorrowful are those who have no love for your lotus feet.
Those whose support is your story ever hold dear the saints and the infinite Lord.
uttar.14.cau7: They have no attachment, no greed, no pride, no arrogance; wealth and misfortune are the same to them.
This is why sages gladly become your servants, and give up for ever their trust in yoga.
uttar.14.cau8: With love they keep their vows unbroken and serve your lotus feet with a pure heart.
Holding scorn and honour alike, all such saints wander the earth in happiness.
uttar.14.cau9: Bee at the lotus of the sages' hearts, O hero of the Raghus, greatly steadfast in battle, unconquered: I worship you.
O Hari, I chant your name and bow to you, the great cure for the disease of worldly existence, the enemy of pride.
uttar.14.cau10: Supreme home of virtue, goodness and grace, lord of Śrī, I bow to you without ceasing.
Joy of the Raghus, root out the mass of opposites; protector of the earth, look upon this humble one.
uttar.14.do14क: Again and again I ask this boon; grant it gladly, lord of Śrī:
unfailing devotion to your lotus feet, and the company of the good for ever.
uttar.14.do14ख: Having told of Śrī Rāma's virtues, Śiva, Umā's lord, went joyfully to Kailāsa.
Then the Lord had the monkeys given lodgings comfortable in every way.
uttar.15.cau1: Listen, Garuḍa: this story is purifying; it destroys the threefold affliction and the fear of worldly existence.
On hearing of the great king's auspicious coronation, people gain dispassion and discernment.
uttar.15.cau2: Those who hear it or sing it with desires in their hearts win happiness and wealth of many kinds.
After enjoying in the world joys rare even for the gods, at the hour of death they go to the city of Śrī Rāma.
uttar.15.cau3: The liberated, the dispassionate and the worldly who hear it gain devotion, the supreme state and ever new wealth.
Garuḍa, I have told the story of Śrī Rāma as far as my own understanding could range; it takes away fear and sorrow.
uttar.15.cau4: It makes dispassion, discernment and devotion firm, and is a fine boat for crossing the river of delusion.
In the city of Kosala there was fresh rejoicing every day, and people of every community were happy.
uttar.15.cau5: Everyone's love for Śrī Rāma's lotus feet, to which Śiva, the sages and Brahmā bow, grew new each day.
Those who came asking were clothed in garments of many kinds, and the Brahmins received gifts of every sort.
uttar.15.do15: All the monkeys were immersed in the bliss of Brahman, and every heart held love for the Lord's feet.
They never noticed the days going by, and six months passed.
uttar.16.cau1: They forgot their homes and did not think of them even in dreams, just as ill will towards others never enters a saint's mind.
Then Śrī Rāma called all his friends; they all came and bowed their heads with respect.
uttar.16.cau2: With the greatest love he seated them close to him and spoke gentle words that gladden devotees:
You have served me greatly. In what words can I praise you to your face?
uttar.16.cau3: That is why you have become so dear to me: for my sake you gave up your homes and their comforts.
My younger brothers, the kingdom, wealth, Sītā, my body, my home, family and loved ones:
uttar.16.cau4: all are dear to me, but none as dear as you. I do not speak falsely; this is my way.
Everyone holds his servant dear, as is the rule; but my love for those who serve me is greater still.
uttar.16.do16: Now go home, all of you, my friends, and worship me with steadfast discipline.
Knowing me as ever present in all and the well-wisher of all, keep loving me dearly.
uttar.17.cau1: Hearing the Lord's words they were all overwhelmed; forgetting who they were and where, they lost all sense of their bodies.
They stood before him with joined palms, gazing without a blink, too full of love to say anything.
uttar.17.cau2: The Lord saw their supreme love and taught them special knowledge in many ways.
Before the Lord they could say nothing, and gazed again and again at his lotus feet.
uttar.17.cau3: Then the Lord sent for ornaments and garments of many colours, matchless and lovely.
Sugrīva was dressed first, Bharata having arranged the garments with his own hands.
uttar.17.cau4: At the Lord's bidding Lakṣmaṇa dressed Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of Laṅkā, who is dear to Śrī Rāma's heart.
Aṅgada stayed seated and did not stir; seeing his love, the Lord did not call him.
uttar.17.do17क: Śrī Rāma dressed Jāmbavān, Nīla and all the others.
Holding Śrī Rāma's form in their hearts and bowing their heads at his feet, they all set off.
uttar.17.do17ख: Then Aṅgada rose and bowed his head, and with tears in his eyes and palms joined
spoke most humbly, in words that seemed steeped in the nectar of love:
uttar.18.cau1: Listen, all-knowing one, ocean of grace and joy, merciful to the lowly, friend of the distressed.
My Lord, when Vāli was dying he left me in your very lap.
uttar.18.cau2: Keep to your proud name as the refuge of those without refuge, and do not forsake me, friend of your devotees.
To me you are master, teacher, father and mother; where could I go, leaving your lotus feet?
uttar.18.cau3: Consider it yourself and tell me, O king of men: leaving my Lord, what business have I at home?
I am a child, without knowledge, sense or strength; keep this humble servant in your refuge, my Lord.
uttar.18.cau4: I will do every lowly task of the household, and by gazing on your lotus feet I shall cross the ocean of worldly existence.
With these words he fell at the Lord's feet and said: Protect me. Do not tell me now to go home, my Lord.
uttar.18.do18क: Śrī Rāma, the very bound of compassion, heard Aṅgada's humble words.
The Lord raised him and clasped him to his heart, his lotus eyes filled with tears.
uttar.18.do18ख: The Lord put the garland from his own breast, robes and jewels on Vāli's son,
and then, after counselling him in many ways, gave him leave to go.
uttar.19.cau1: Mindful of what the devotees had done, Bharata went with his younger brother Śatrughna and Lakṣmaṇa to see them off.
No small love filled Aṅgada's heart; again and again he turned to look towards Śrī Rāma,
uttar.19.cau2: and again and again he prostrated himself, hoping in his heart that Śrī Rāma would tell him to stay.
Remembering over and over how Śrī Rāma looked, spoke, walked and met him with a smile, he grieved.
uttar.19.cau3: Seeing the Lord's wish, he made many humble entreaties and went on his way, holding the lotus feet in his heart.
Bharata escorted all the monkeys with great honour, and then returned with his brothers.
uttar.19.cau4: Then Hanumān clasped Sugrīva's feet and pleaded with him in many ways:
Let me serve at Śrī Rāma's feet for ten days, my lord, and then I shall come and see your feet again.
uttar.19.cau5: Sugrīva said: Son of the Wind, you are a store of merit; go and serve the Lord, the home of grace.
With these words all the monkeys left at once. Aṅgada said: Listen, Hanumān:
uttar.19.do19क: Give the Lord my prostrations; I ask you this with joined palms.
And keep reminding Śrī Rāma of me, again and again.
uttar.19.do19ख: With these words Vāli's son went on his way, and Hanumān came back.
He told the Lord of Aṅgada's love, and the Lord was overcome with it.
uttar.19.do19ग: Harder than the thunderbolt and gentler far than a flower:
such is Śrī Rāma's heart, Garuḍa. Tell me, who can understand it?
uttar.20.cau1: Then the compassionate Lord sent for the Niṣāda chief, bestowed ornaments and garments on him as a blessing, and said:
Go home, keep me in remembrance, and follow dharma in thought, deed and word.
uttar.20.cau2: You are my friend, and a brother to me like Bharata; keep coming to the city always.
On hearing this he was filled with great joy, and fell at the Lord's feet with tears in his eyes.
uttar.20.cau3: Holding the Lord's lotus feet in his heart he went home, and told his family of the Lord's nature.
Seeing Śrī Rāma's ways, the citizens said again and again: Blessed is the Lord, the treasure of joy.
uttar.20.cau4: When Śrī Rāma took his seat on the throne, the three worlds rejoiced and all their sorrows left them.
Nobody held a grudge against another; through Śrī Rāma's power all strife was gone.
uttar.20.do20: The people were each devoted to the dharma of their own class (varṇa) and stage of life (āśrama).
They always walked the path of the Veda and lived in happiness, with no fear, no grief and no disease.
uttar.21.cau1: In Śrī Rāma's kingdom no one was touched by the afflictions that come from the body, from the gods or from other creatures.
Everyone loved one another, and each walked devoted to his own dharma as the Veda directs.
uttar.21.cau2: Dharma stood on all its four feet throughout the world; there was no sin, not even in dreams.
Every man and woman was given to devotion to Śrī Rāma, and all were fit for the supreme state.
uttar.21.cau3: There was no untimely death and no pain of any kind; all were handsome, and all were sound and free of disease in body.
No one was poor, unhappy or wretched; no one was ignorant or without auspicious marks.
uttar.21.cau4: All were free of hypocrisy, given to dharma and virtuous; men and women alike were skilful and accomplished.
All knew the worth of merit, all were learned and wise, all were grateful, and none was clever in deceit.
uttar.21.do21: Listen, Garuḍa: in Śrī Rāma's kingdom, throughout the world of moving and unmoving beings,
no one suffered sorrow caused by time, karma, nature or the guṇas.
uttar.22.cau1: Śrī Rāma of Kosala was the one king of the earth, girdled by the seven seas.
Yet for him in each of whose hairs lie many worlds, this lordship was no great thing.
uttar.22.cau2: Once that greatness of the Lord is understood, to describe this is to belittle him greatly.
Yet, Garuḍa, the very ones who know that greatness find their joy in this story once more.
uttar.22.cau3: Great sages of subdued senses declare that this play is the very fruit of knowing that greatness.
The happiness and wealth of Śrī Rāma's reign neither Śeṣa, king of serpents, nor Sarasvatī could describe.
uttar.22.cau4: All were generous, all did good to others; men and women all served at the feet of the Brahmins.
Every man kept the vow of one wife, and wives sought their husbands' good in thought, word and deed.
uttar.22.do22: Daṇḍa, the rod, was found only in the hands of ascetics, and bheda, division, only in the dance of a troupe of dancers;
and conquest was heard of only as conquest of the mind: such was the reign of Śrī Rāma.
uttar.23.cau1: The forest trees were ever in flower and in fruit, and the elephant and the lion shared one place.
Bird and beast laid aside the enmity born in them, and love grew up among them all.
uttar.23.cau2: Birds sang, and herds of beasts of many kinds roamed the forest without fear, rejoicing.
A cool, fragrant breeze blew gently, and bees went humming, carrying the nectar of flowers.
uttar.23.cau3: When asked, creepers and trees dripped honey, and the cows yielded whatever milk was wished for.
The land stayed full of harvest at all times; the Tretā age took on the ways of the Kṛta age.
uttar.23.cau4: Mines of many kinds of gems appeared in the mountains, which knew the king for the soul of the world.
Every river ran with the best of water, cool and clear, delightful to drink.
uttar.23.cau5: The seas stayed within their limits and left gems along the shore, which men picked up.
Every pond was crowded with lotuses, and all the ten quarters were bright and glad.
uttar.23.do23: The moon steeped the earth in its rays, and the sun burned no more than the need called for;
clouds gave rain when it was asked for, in the reign of Śrī Rāma.
uttar.24.cau1: The Lord performed millions of horse sacrifices and gave many gifts to the Brahmins.
He guards the path of the Vedas and is foremost in upholding dharma; he is beyond the guṇas, and in enjoyment he is like Indra.
uttar.24.cau2: Sītā is always at one with her husband's wishes; she is a mine of beauty, gentle-natured and humble.
She knows the greatness of the Lord, the ocean of mercy, and serves his lotus feet with her whole heart.
uttar.24.cau3: Though there are many servants, men and women, in the house, all of them ever skilled in the ways of service,
yet Sītā does the work of the house with her own hands and follows Śrī Rāma's every command.
uttar.24.cau4: Whatever way pleases the Lord, the ocean of mercy, Śrī (Sītā), knowing the ways of service, does just that.
She serves all her mothers-in-law in the house, Kausalyā and the rest, with no pride and no vanity in her.
uttar.24.cau5: Umā, she is Ramā, to whom Brahmā and the other gods bow; she is the Mother of the world, ever beyond reproach.
uttar.24.do24: She whose glance of grace the gods long for, and who does not so much as look at them,
sets that nature of hers aside and loves the lotus feet of Śrī Rāma.
uttar.25.cau1: All the brothers serve him in keeping with his wishes, and their love for Śrī Rāma's feet is exceedingly great.
They keep their eyes on the Lord's lotus face, waiting for the compassionate Lord to ask something of them some day.
uttar.25.cau2: Śrī Rāma loves his brothers and teaches them right counsel in many ways.
The people of the city live in joy and enjoy every pleasure, such as even the gods can hardly find.
uttar.25.cau3: Day and night they keep praying to Brahmā, asking for love for the feet of Śrī Rāma.
Two beautiful sons were born to Sītā, Lava and Kuśa, whose praises the Vedas and Purāṇas sing.
uttar.25.cau4: Both are victorious, modest and abodes of virtue, so beautiful that they seem reflections of Śrī Hari himself.
Each of the brothers had two sons, rich in beauty, virtue and good character.
uttar.25.do25: He who is beyond knowledge, speech and the senses, the unborn, who is beyond māyā, the mind and the guṇas,
he, who is being, consciousness and bliss in full, is acting out a noble human life.
uttar.26.cau1: At daybreak, after bathing in the Sarayū, he sits in the assembly with Brahmins and good men.
Vasiṣṭha expounds the Vedas and Purāṇas, and Śrī Rāma listens, though he knows it all.
uttar.26.cau2: He eats together with his younger brothers, and seeing this every mother's heart brims with happiness.
The two brothers Bharata and Śatrughna go to the grove with Hanumān, son of the Wind.
uttar.26.cau3: Sitting there, they ask for the story of Śrī Rāma's virtues, and Hanumān, wise of mind, dives deep into them and tells it.
Hearing of those spotless virtues they are filled with joy, and entreat him to tell them again and again.
uttar.26.cau4: In every home Purāṇas are recited and Śrī Rāma's holy deeds are told in many ways.
Men and women go on singing Śrī Rāma's virtues, and so doing they never notice the days and nights go by.
uttar.26.do26: All the store of happiness and wealth of the people of Ayodhyā
a thousand Śeṣas could not describe, for there Śrī Rāma reigns as king.
uttar.27.cau1: Nārada, Sanaka and other great sages, to see the Lord of Kosala,
come to Ayodhyā every day, and at the sight of the city they forget their dispassion.
uttar.27.cau2: The upper storeys are built of gold and gems, with lovely floors cast in many colours.
Round the city runs a wall of great beauty, crowned with fine battlements of every colour.
uttar.27.cau3: It is as if the hosts of the nine planets had formed an army and come to lay siege to Amarāvatī.
The ground is paved with glass of many colours, and seeing it even the minds of great sages dance.
uttar.27.cau4: The white mansions kiss the sky above, and their pinnacles seem to scorn the brilliance of the sun and moon.
Windows wrought of many gems sparkle, and in every house lamps of gems glow.
uttar.27.cha1: Lamps of gems shine, the mansions gleam, and the thresholds are made of coral.
There are pillars of gems, and walls fashioned by Brahmā himself, inlaid with gold, gems and emeralds.
The mansions are beautiful, charming and spacious, and their courtyards are built of lovely crystal.
At every single gateway the doors are of gold, finely wrought and set with many diamonds.
uttar.27.do27: In every house there are lovely picture halls, where the deeds of Śrī Rāma are painted with great art;
any sage who gazes at them has his heart stolen away.
uttar.28.cau1: Everyone has planted flower gardens and laid them out with care in many styles.
In them graceful creepers of many kinds, lovely to see, are always in bloom, as if it were spring.
uttar.28.cau2: Bees hum with a sweet and charming sound, and a pleasant breeze, cool, gentle and fragrant, is always blowing.
Children have reared birds of many kinds, which speak sweetly and look lovely as they fly.
uttar.28.cau3: Peacocks, swans, cranes and pigeons look splendid upon the mansions.
Seeing their own reflections here and there, they call in many ways and dance.
uttar.28.cau4: Children teach the parrots and mynas: Say Rāma, Raghupati, protector of his people.
The royal gateway is beautiful in every way, and so are the streets, the crossroads and the markets.
uttar.28.cha1: The lovely markets are beyond describing; there goods are had without payment.
Where he in whom Ramā dwells is himself king, how could the wealth of the place be sung?
Cloth dealers, bankers and many merchants sit there, as though each were Kubera.
Women, men, children and the old, whoever they are, are all happy, all upright and fair to see.
uttar.28.do28: On the northern side flows the Sarayū, its water clear and deep.
Charming ghats are built along it, and there is not the least mud on its banks.
uttar.29.cau1: Far off, in an open place, is a fine ghat where troops of horses and elephants drink.
There are many ghats for drawing water, most charming, and there men do not bathe.
uttar.29.cau2: The royal ghat is fine and beautiful in every way; there men of all four varṇas bathe.
All along the bank stand temples of the gods, with lovely groves on every side of them.
uttar.29.cau3: At spots along the riverside dwell sages and renunciants who have turned from the world and delight in knowledge.
Lovely tulasī lines the banks, set out clump by clump by many sages.
uttar.29.cau4: The beauty of the city cannot be told at all, and outside the city too all is supremely lovely.
At the sight of the city every sin takes flight; there are woods, groves, stepwells and lakes.
uttar.29.cha1: Peerless stepwells, lakes and wells, charming and wide, add to its beauty.
Seeing their fine steps and clear water, gods and sages are entranced.
Lotuses of many colours grow there, many birds call and bees hum.
The delightful gardens, with the songs of cuckoos and other birds, seem to call out to the passers-by.
uttar.29.do29: Can the city whose king is the Lord of Ramā be described?
Aṇimā and the other powers, and all joys and riches, fill the whole of Ayodhyā.
uttar.30.cau1: Everywhere people sing Śrī Rāma's virtues, and as they sit together they urge this upon one another:
Worship Śrī Rāma, who cherishes those who bow to him, the home of beauty, good character, grace of form and every virtue.
uttar.30.cau2: Worship him whose eyes are lotuses and whose body is dark, who guards his servants as the eyelids guard the eyes.
Worship him who bears lovely arrows, bow and quiver, the sun to the lotus grove of the saints, steadfast in battle.
uttar.30.cau3: Worship him who is Garuḍa to the terrible serpent of Time, who wipes out the sense of mine in all who bow to him free of desire.
Worship him who is the hunter of the herd of deer, greed and delusion, a lion to the elephant of desire, and the giver of joy to his devotees.
uttar.30.cau4: He is the sun to the thick darkness of doubt and grief, and the fire that burns the dense forest of the demons.
